en_zh_a1_2_ji_duoshao.helpMemoryIntro: Two ways to ask "how many": 几 for small countable numbers (expects <10, needs a measure word), 多少 for anything (measure word optional).

helpMemoryTips.title: 几 + MW, 多少 free
helpMemoryTips.text: 几口人? 几本书? — 几 always carries the measure word. 多少钱? 多少人? — 多少 doesn't need one.

helpMemoryTips.title: 几 also tells time
helpMemoryTips.text: 几点? = what time? (literally "how-many o'clock") — coming in the next module.

en_zh_a1_2_listen_family.title: Listening: 我的家
en_zh_a1_2_listen_family.helpMemoryIntro: Listen to Xiaomei describe her family. Catch the counting word 口 and who does what.

helpMemoryTips.title: 口 counts family members
helpMemoryTips.text: Family size uses the measure word 口 (mouth): 五口人 = five mouths to feed. Anywhere else, people take 个.

en_zh_a1_2_listen_family.readingPassage: 我家有五口人：爸爸、妈妈、哥哥、妹妹和我。我爸爸是医生，我妈妈是老师。我哥哥很高，我妹妹很小。我们家有一只猫，它叫花花。我很爱我的家。
en_zh_a1_2_listen_family.readingPassageTranslation:
Wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén: bàba, māma, gēge, mèimei hé wǒ. Wǒ bàba shì yīshēng, wǒ māma shì lǎoshī. Wǒ gēge hěn gāo, wǒ mèimei hěn xiǎo. Wǒmen jiā yǒu yì zhī māo, tā jiào Huāhua. Wǒ hěn ài wǒ de jiā.

There are five people in my family: dad, mum, my older brother, my younger sister and me. My dad is a doctor, my mum is a teacher. My brother is tall; my little sister is small. Our family has a cat called Huahua. I love my family very much.

readingQuestions.question: 小美家有几口人？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How many people are in Xiaomei's family?

en_zh_a1_2_read_friend.title: Reading: 我的朋友小美
en_zh_a1_2_read_friend.helpMemoryIntro: Meet 小美, Tom's friend. Everything here uses this module's grammar: 很 + adjective, 的, 有/没有, and the measure words 个 and 只.

helpMemoryTips.title: 可是 = but
helpMemoryTips.text: The passage ends with 可是 (but) — your first sentence connector. 但是 is its slightly more formal twin.

en_zh_a1_2_read_friend.readingPassage: 小美是我的好朋友。她是中国人，她家在北京。小美很高，也很好看。她有一个弟弟，他叫小明。小明很小，他不是学生。小美家有一只白色的猫。我很喜欢小美的猫，可是我没有猫。
en_zh_a1_2_read_friend.readingPassageTranslation:
Xiǎoměi shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou. Tā shì Zhōngguó rén, tā jiā zài Běijīng. Xiǎoměi hěn gāo, yě hěn hǎokàn. Tā yǒu yí ge dìdi, tā jiào Xiǎomíng. Xiǎomíng hěn xiǎo, tā bú shì xuésheng. Xiǎoměi jiā yǒu yì zhī báisè de māo. Wǒ hěn xǐhuan Xiǎoměi de māo, kěshì wǒ méiyǒu māo.

Xiaomei is my good friend. She's Chinese and her family lives in Beijing. Xiaomei is tall and also pretty. She has a younger brother called Xiaoming. Xiaoming is little; he's not a student yet. Xiaomei's family has a white cat. I really like Xiaomei's cat — but I don't have a cat.

readingQuestions.question: 小美的弟弟叫什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What is Xiaomei's younger brother called?

readingQuestions.question: 谁没有猫？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does not have a cat?

en_zh_a1_2_read_home.title: Reading: 这是我的家
en_zh_a1_2_read_home.helpMemoryIntro: Tom introduces his family. Notice 也 (also) sliding in before the verb: 我妈妈**也**是医生.

helpMemoryTips.title: 也 sits before the verb
helpMemoryTips.text: "Too/also" is 也, and it always lands in front of the verb: 她也是学生 — never at the end like English "too".

en_zh_a1_2_read_home.readingPassage: 你好！我叫汤姆。这是我的家。我家有四口人：爸爸、妈妈、姐姐和我。我爸爸是英国人，他是医生。我妈妈也是医生。我姐姐是学生，她很高。我们家有一只狗，它叫Max。我很爱我的家。
en_zh_a1_2_read_home.readingPassageTranslation:
Nǐ hǎo! Wǒ jiào Tāngmǔ. Zhè shì wǒ de jiā. Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén: bàba, māma, jiějie hé wǒ. Wǒ bàba shì Yīngguó rén, tā shì yīshēng. Wǒ māma yě shì yīshēng. Wǒ jiějie shì xuésheng, tā hěn gāo. Wǒmen jiā yǒu yì zhī gǒu, tā jiào Max. Wǒ hěn ài wǒ de jiā.

Hello! I'm Tom. This is my family. There are four of us: dad, mum, my older sister and me. My dad is British — he's a doctor. My mum is a doctor too. My sister is a student, and she's tall. We have a dog called Max. I love my family very much.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆家有几口人？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How many people are in Tom's family?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆的妈妈是做什么的？

en_zh_a1_2_speak_family.title: Speaking: my family

subjects.english: Wǒ jiā yǒu sì kǒu rén. — There are four of us in my family.
Zhè shì wǒ bàba. — This is my dad.
Wǒ māma shì lǎoshī. — My mum is a teacher.
Wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge. — I have an older brother.
Wǒ méiyǒu mèimei. — I don't have a younger sister.
Wǒmen jiā yǒu yì zhī māo. — Our family has a cat.

en_zh_a1_2_speak_family.helpMemoryIntro: Talk about your family — listen and repeat, watching the tones.

helpMemoryTips.title: One breath per sentence
helpMemoryTips.text: These sentences are short on purpose: say each in one relaxed breath, keeping every syllable's tone — speed comes later.

en_zh_a1_2_speak_sandhi.title: Tones in real words

subjects.english: wǒ hěn hǎo → "wó hén hǎo" — I'm fine
nǐ yě hǎo — you're good too (another chain)
wǒ xiǎng mǎi shuǐ — I want to buy water
jiějie hěn máng — older sister is busy
wǒ jiā yǒu wǔ kǒu rén — five in my family (careful: 五口 stays 3+3→2+3)

en_zh_a1_2_speak_sandhi.helpMemoryIntro: The sandhi rules from A1.1, now inside real phrases — including chains of third tones. Say them at natural speed.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Sandhi is automatic, pinyin isn't (Z2)
helpMemoryTips.text: Pinyin keeps writing nǐ hǎo with two dips — your mouth converts the first to a rise. Read pinyin with your ears, not your eyes.

helpMemoryTips.title: Keep the last dip low
helpMemoryTips.text: In a 3+3 pair only the FIRST syllable changes. The final third tone stays a low dip — don't lift it.

helpMemoryTips.title: Compounds are building blocks
helpMemoryTips.text: 电 electric: 电脑 electric-brain = computer, 电视 electric-see = TV. Decode the parts and half your vocabulary is free.

en_zh_a1_2_this_that.helpMemoryIntro: 这 zhè = this (near), 那 nà = that (far), 哪 nǎ = which (the question twin). Pointing at things needs the measure word too: 这个, 那本.

helpMemoryTips.title: nà = that, nǎ = which?
helpMemoryTips.text: Same character family, different tone: falling 那 points (that), dipping 哪 asks (which?). The tone IS the grammar here.

helpMemoryTips.title: 这/那 + MW + noun
helpMemoryTips.text: Pointing at a specific thing takes the measure word: 这个人 this person, 那本书 that book — same suitcase rule as numbers (Z11).

en_zh_a1_2_you_ge.helpMemoryIntro: 有 yǒu = to have / there is. And counting anything needs a measure word between the number and the noun: 一**个**人, never 一人.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Every noun brings its suitcase (Z11)
helpMemoryTips.text: Number (or 这/那) + MEASURE WORD + noun, always. 个 gè is the all-purpose suitcase — when in doubt, 个. English already does this with "a CUP of tea, a PAIR of trousers".

helpMemoryTips.title: 有 negates with 没 (Z18)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我有猫 I have a cat → 我**没**有猫 I don't. Never 不有 — 有 is the one verb that refuses 不.

en_zh_a2_1_calendar.helpMemoryIntro: Weekdays are numbered (星期一 = weekday-one = Monday), months are numbered (二月 = two-month = February). Two patterns replace fourteen English words.

helpMemoryTips.title: Count your week
helpMemoryTips.text: 星期一 Monday … 星期六 Saturday — then Sunday breaks the pattern: 星期天 (or 星期日), the "sky/sun day".

helpMemoryTips.title: Dates run big → small
helpMemoryTips.text: Year 年 → month 月 → day 号 → weekday: 2026年7月2号星期四. Chinese time always zooms from large to small.

helpMemoryTips.title: Verb + built-in object

helpMemoryTips.title: Frequency lives in the WHEN slot (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我常常喝茶, 他每天上班 — same position as 明天 or 七点. One slot to rule all time words.

en_zh_a2_1_hui_neng.helpMemoryIntro: English "can" splits three ways: 会 = learned skill, 能 = physically/circumstantially able, 可以 = allowed.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Skill 会, power 能, permission 可以 (Z26)
helpMemoryTips.text: Learned it? 会 (我会说中文). Able right now? 能 (今天我不能来). Allowed? 可以 (这儿可以坐吗?). Pick by asking WHY you "can".

helpMemoryTips.title: 会 also predicts
helpMemoryTips.text: Later, 会 marks likely futures: 明天会下雨 — it will rain. Skill first, forecast later.

en_zh_a2_1_listen_morning.title: Listening: 你几点起床?
en_zh_a2_1_listen_morning.helpMemoryIntro: Listen for the times — they always come right before the action they schedule.

helpMemoryTips.title: Numbers first
helpMemoryTips.text: Catch 七点, 七点半, 八点, 十二点 — pin each time to the verb that follows it and the whole story falls into place.

en_zh_a2_1_listen_morning.readingPassage: 汤姆每天早上七点起床。他七点半喝咖啡，吃面包。八点他去学校学习中文。他很喜欢他的中文课。十二点他和小美在学校吃午饭。
en_zh_a2_1_listen_morning.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng. Tā qī diǎn bàn hē kāfēi, chī miànbāo. Bā diǎn tā qù xuéxiào xuéxí Zhōngwén. Tā hěn xǐhuan tā de Zhōngwén kè. Shí'èr diǎn tā hé Xiǎoměi zài xuéxiào chī wǔfàn.

Tom gets up at seven every morning. At 7:30 he drinks coffee and eats bread. At eight he goes to school to study Chinese. He really likes his Chinese class. At twelve he and Xiaomei eat lunch at school.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆几点起床？

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆早上喝什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom drink in the morning?

readingQuestions.question: 他和谁吃午饭？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does he eat lunch with?

en_zh_a2_1_listen_weekend.title: Listening: 周末做什么?
en_zh_a2_1_listen_weekend.helpMemoryIntro: Xiaomei's weekend. Listen once for the days, once for what happens on each.

helpMemoryTips.title: Weekend = 周末
helpMemoryTips.text: 周 is the formal "week": 周末 weekend, 周一 = 星期一 Monday. You'll hear both systems everywhere.

en_zh_a2_1_listen_weekend.readingPassage: 我周末不上课。星期六早上我常常去咖啡馆看书。下午我喜欢和朋友去公园。星期天我在家。早上我给妈妈打电话，下午我做饭。我会做很多中国菜。晚上我有时候看电视，十点半睡觉。
en_zh_a2_1_listen_weekend.readingPassageTranslation:
Wǒ zhōumò bú shàngkè. Xīngqīliù zǎoshang wǒ chángcháng qù kāfēiguǎn kàn shū. Xiàwǔ wǒ xǐhuan hé péngyou qù gōngyuán. Xīngqītiān wǒ zài jiā. Zǎoshang wǒ gěi māma dǎ diànhuà, xiàwǔ wǒ zuòfàn. Wǒ huì zuò hěn duō Zhōngguó cài. Wǎnshang wǒ yǒushíhou kàn diànshì, shí diǎn bàn shuìjiào.

I don't have class at the weekend. On Saturday morning I often go to the café to read. In the afternoon I like going to the park with friends. On Sunday I stay home. In the morning I phone my mum; in the afternoon I cook. I can make lots of Chinese dishes. In the evening I sometimes watch TV, and I go to bed at half past ten.

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who does she phone on Sunday morning?

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What time does she go to bed?

en_zh_a2_1_qu_verb.helpMemoryIntro: Verbs chain directly in Chinese: 去买咖啡 = go buy coffee. No "to", no linking word — the second verb is the purpose of the first.

helpMemoryTips.title: Verbs stack bare (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我去学校学习中文 — go + study, no connector. English needs "to"; Chinese just lines the actions up in order of happening.

en_zh_a2_1_read_cafe.title: Reading: 在咖啡馆
en_zh_a2_1_read_cafe.helpMemoryIntro: Your first dialogue. Notice how the answer to a Chinese question keeps the question's exact shape — 能…吗? → 能!

helpMemoryTips.title: Answer with the verb
helpMemoryTips.text: Chinese has no yes/no words: answer by echoing the verb. 能吗? → 能 / 不能. 想去吗? → 想 / 不想.

en_zh_a2_1_read_cafe.readingPassage:
星期六早上，汤姆和小美在咖啡馆。
小美："你想喝什么？"
汤姆："我要一杯咖啡。你呢？"
小美："我不喝咖啡，我要一杯茶。"
汤姆："你今天下午想做什么？"
小美："我想去书店买书，你能和我一起去吗？"
汤姆："能！我也想买一本中文书。"
en_zh_a2_1_read_cafe.readingPassageTranslation:
Xīngqīliù zǎoshang, Tāngmǔ hé Xiǎoměi zài kāfēiguǎn.
Xiǎoměi: "Nǐ xiǎng hē shénme?"
Tāngmǔ: "Wǒ yào yì bēi kāfēi. Nǐ ne?"
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ bù hē kāfēi, wǒ yào yì bēi chá."
Tāngmǔ: "Nǐ jīntiān xiàwǔ xiǎng zuò shénme?"
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ xiǎng qù shūdiàn mǎi shū, nǐ néng hé wǒ yìqǐ qù ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Néng! Wǒ yě xiǎng mǎi yì běn Zhōngwén shū."

Saturday morning, Tom and Xiaomei are at the café.
Xiaomei: "What would you like to drink?"
Tom: "I'll have a coffee. You?"
Xiaomei: "I don't drink coffee — I'll have a tea."
Tom: "What do you want to do this afternoon?"
Xiaomei: "I'd like to go to the bookshop to buy books. Can you come with me?"
Tom: "I can! I'd like to buy a Chinese book too."

readingQuestions.question: 小美下午想去哪儿？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Where does Xiaomei want to go in the afternoon?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想买什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom want to buy?

en_zh_a2_1_read_day.title: Reading: 汤姆的一天
en_zh_a2_1_read_day.helpMemoryIntro: A full day, scheduled the Chinese way: every time and place stands before its verb. Read it twice — once for the story, once for the word order.

helpMemoryTips.title: Spot the pattern (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: Underline mentally: 七点起床, 在学校学习, 晚上六点回家 — WHEN/WHERE + verb, sentence after sentence. That rhythm is the grammar.

en_zh_a2_1_read_day.readingPassage: 汤姆每天早上七点起床，七点半喝咖啡。八点他去学校，在学校学习中文。十二点他和朋友吃午饭。下午他在图书馆看书。晚上六点他回家做饭。他会做英国菜，可是他更想学做中国菜。晚上他有时候看电视，有时候给妈妈打电话。他十一点睡觉。
en_zh_a2_1_read_day.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ měitiān zǎoshang qī diǎn qǐchuáng, qī diǎn bàn hē kāfēi. Bā diǎn tā qù xuéxiào, zài xuéxiào xuéxí Zhōngwén. Shí'èr diǎn tā hé péngyou chī wǔfàn. Xiàwǔ tā zài túshūguǎn kàn shū. Wǎnshang liù diǎn tā huí jiā zuòfàn. Tā huì zuò Yīngguó cài, kěshì tā gèng xiǎng xué zuò Zhōngguó cài. Wǎnshang tā yǒushíhou kàn diànshì, yǒushíhou gěi māma dǎ diànhuà. Tā shíyī diǎn shuìjiào.

Tom gets up at seven every morning and drinks coffee at 7:30. At eight he goes to school, where he studies Chinese. At twelve he eats lunch with friends. In the afternoon he reads in the library. At six in the evening he goes home and cooks. He can cook British food, but he'd rather learn to cook Chinese food. In the evening he sometimes watches TV, sometimes phones his mum. He goes to bed at eleven.

readingQuestions.question: 下午他做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does he do in the afternoon?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想学做什么菜？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What food does Tom want to learn to cook?

en_zh_a2_1_speak_day.title: Speaking: my day

subjects.english: Wǒ měitiān qī diǎn qǐchuáng. — I get up at seven every day.
Wǒ zǎoshang hē kāfēi. — I drink coffee in the morning.
Wǒ bā diǎn bàn qù xuéxiào. — I go to school at 8:30.
Wǒmen shí'èr diǎn chī wǔfàn. — We eat lunch at twelve.
Wǎnshang wǒ kàn diànshì. — In the evening I watch TV.
Wǒ shíyī diǎn shuìjiào. — I go to bed at eleven.

en_zh_a2_1_speak_day.helpMemoryIntro: Say your daily routine aloud — feel how the time expression always lands before the action.

helpMemoryTips.title: Chunk it: WHEN + DO
helpMemoryTips.text: Pause mentally after the time chunk: 我七点 // 起床. Building the habit aloud installs the word order for free (Z13).

en_zh_a2_1_speak_finals.title: Sounds: -n vs -ng, j/q/x, ü

subjects.english: j q x: jiā qī xiǎo — home, seven, small
ü after j/q/x: qù jǔ xǔ
Wǒ xiǎng qù Zhōngguó. — I'd like to go to China.

en_zh_a2_1_speak_finals.helpMemoryIntro: Three sound contrasts English ears blur: the -n/-ng endings, the smiling j/q/x row, and ü. Exaggerate them now, relax later.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ fán ≠ fáng (Z5)
helpMemoryTips.text: -n ends with the tongue tip at the teeth; -ng ends open, in the throat. 半 bàn vs 帮 bāng, 人 rén vs 冷 lěng — different words.

helpMemoryTips.title: ü = "ee" with rounded lips
helpMemoryTips.text: Say "ee", freeze your tongue, round your lips: 去 qù, 女 nǚ, 绿 lǜ. After j/q/x it's written u but still sounds ü.

en_zh_a2_1_time.helpMemoryIntro: Clock time is number + 点 (o'clock): 三点 = 3:00. Add 半 for half past and 分 for minutes. 几点? asks the time.

helpMemoryTips.title: 点 = o'clock, 半 = half past
helpMemoryTips.text: 八点 8:00, 八点半 8:30, 八点十分 8:10. Note "two o'clock" is 两点 (liǎng diǎn), never 二点.

en_zh_a2_1_word_order.helpMemoryIntro: The word-order cliff: English says "I get up at seven"; Chinese sets the scene first — 我七点起床 (I at-seven get up). Time never trails the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Set the scene, then act (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: Subject + WHEN + (WHERE) + verb: 我明天去北京. Putting time at the end (我去北京明天 ✗) is the #1 English-speaker word-order error.

helpMemoryTips.title: Time can also lead
helpMemoryTips.text: For emphasis the time may open the sentence: 明天我去北京. Before the subject or after it — but never after the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: 想 wishes, 要 orders
helpMemoryTips.text: 我想喝茶 I feel like tea; 我要喝茶 I WANT tea / I'm having tea. In a café, 我要一杯咖啡 is how you actually order.

helpMemoryTips.title: 想 + noun = to miss
helpMemoryTips.text: 我想你 = I miss you — 想 straight onto a person means missing them, not wanting them to do something.

helpMemoryTips.title: 在 alone = to be at

en_zh_a2_2_guo.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 过 guo marks life experience: 我去过中国 — I've been to China (at some point). Negate with 没…过 — and the 过 stays!

helpMemoryTips.title: 过 = the passport stamp (Z15)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了 stamps ONE completed event; 过 stamps your passport: "this experience exists in my life". 你吃过北京烤鸭吗? — Have you ever had Peking duck?

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 没 keeps 过 (unlike 了)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我没去过中国 — the 过 survives negation: "the experience is missing". Compare 我没买书, where 了 disappears.

en_zh_a2_2_le_change.helpMemoryIntro: Sentence-final 了 stamps a CHANGE: 下雨了 — it's raining (now); 我累了 — I've gotten tired. Something is different from before.

helpMemoryTips.title: End-of-sentence 了 = "new now" (Z14)
helpMemoryTips.text: 他是学生了 — he's a student NOW (he wasn't). 我不喝咖啡了 — I don't drink coffee ANYMORE. The 了 says: update your picture.

helpMemoryTips.title: Two 了s, two jobs
helpMemoryTips.text: Verb-了 = action completed (买了). Sentence-了 = situation changed (下雨了). One character, two stamps — context tells you which.

en_zh_a2_2_le_done.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 了 stamps an action as completed: 我买了一本书 — I bought a book. It's a ✓-stamp, not a past tense: habits and states never take it.

helpMemoryTips.title: A ✓-stamp, not a tense (Z14)
helpMemoryTips.text: Ask "did the action complete?" — if yes, stamp the verb: 吃了, 买了, 去了. If you're describing a habit or a state, no stamp.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Past ≠ 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 昨天我很忙 (yesterday I was busy) has NO 了 — 忙 is a state, nothing completed. 每天…了 ✗ too: habits aren't single completed events. This is the #1 error at every level.

en_zh_a2_2_listen_eaten.title: Listening: 你吃饭了吗?
en_zh_a2_2_listen_eaten.helpMemoryIntro: 你吃饭了吗? is also a classic Chinese greeting. Listen for 了, 过 and 还没 doing their different jobs.

helpMemoryTips.title: The greeting that isn't a question
helpMemoryTips.text: 你吃了吗? between neighbours just means "hi". Here it's a real question — context decides.

en_zh_a2_2_listen_eaten.readingPassage:
小美："汤姆，你吃午饭了吗？"
汤姆："还没呢。我早上只喝了一杯咖啡。"
小美："我知道一个很好的饭馆。你吃过中国菜吗？"
汤姆："吃过，可是我没吃过北京烤鸭。"
小美："那我们今天去吃烤鸭吧！"
汤姆："太好了！我们走吧。"
en_zh_a2_2_listen_eaten.readingPassageTranslation:
Xiǎoměi: "Tāngmǔ, nǐ chī wǔfàn le ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Hái méi ne. Wǒ zǎoshang zhǐ hē le yì bēi kāfēi."
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒ zhīdào yí ge hěn hǎo de fànguǎn. Nǐ chī guo Zhōngguó cài ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Chī guo, kěshì wǒ méi chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā."
Xiǎoměi: "Nà wǒmen jīntiān qù chī kǎoyā ba!"
Tāngmǔ: "Tài hǎo le! Wǒmen zǒu ba."

Xiaomei: "Tom, have you had lunch?"
Tom: "Not yet. I only had a coffee this morning."
Xiaomei: "I know a great restaurant. Have you ever had Chinese food?"
Tom: "I have — but I've never had Peking duck."
Xiaomei: "Then let's go eat duck today!"
Tom: "Great! Let's go."

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆早上喝了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Tom drink in the morning?

en_zh_a2_2_measure_words.helpMemoryIntro: Beyond 个: nouns sort by shape and kind. 本 for bound things, 张 for flat things, 条 for long bendy things, 只 for animals, 杯 cups, 瓶 bottles, 件 clothes-tops, 双 pairs, 辆 vehicles, 位 people (polite).

helpMemoryTips.title: Sort by shape (Z11)
helpMemoryTips.text: Bound pages → 本. Flat sheet → 张. Long & bendy → 条. On legs → 只. Politely human → 位. When truly lost, 个 still works — but each right suitcase earns you fluency points.

helpMemoryTips.title: English does this too
helpMemoryTips.text: A PAIR of trousers, a SHEET of paper, a CUP of tea — English partitives are measure words in disguise. Chinese just applies them to every noun.

en_zh_a2_2_mei.helpMemoryIntro: To say something DIDN'T happen, use 没(有) before the verb — and drop the 了: 我没买书. 不 keeps its jobs: habits, futures, states.

helpMemoryTips.title: 没 for done-and-have, 不 for everything else (Z17)
helpMemoryTips.text: 没 negates completed events (没去 didn't go) and 有. 不 negates habits (不喝咖啡), futures (明天不去), adjectives (不累) and willingness.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 没 kills the 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我没买了书 ✗ — once 没 says "not completed", the ✓-stamp 了 must go: 我没买书. They never appear together.

en_zh_a2_2_read_shopping.title: Reading: 买东西
en_zh_a2_2_read_shopping.helpMemoryIntro: Tom haggles. Track the measure words (件, 瓶) and the money — and note 零 in 一百零六 (one hundred **and** six).

helpMemoryTips.title: 零 plugs the gap
helpMemoryTips.text: 106 = 一百零六 — the 零 (zero) marks the skipped tens place. 160 would be 一百六(十).

en_zh_a2_2_read_shopping.readingPassage:
今天下午汤姆去商店买东西。他想买一件衬衫。
汤姆："你好，这件白色的衬衫多少钱？"
售货员："一百二十块。"
汤姆："太贵了！能便宜一点儿吗？"
售货员："一百块，怎么样？"
汤姆："好，我买了。我还要两瓶水。"
售货员："一共一百零六块。"

Jīntiān xiàwǔ Tāngmǔ qù shāngdiàn mǎi dōngxi. Tā xiǎng mǎi yí jiàn chènshān.

Tāngmǔ: "Tài guì le! Néng piányi yìdiǎnr ma?"

en_zh_a2_2_read_weekend.title: Reading: 汤姆的周末
en_zh_a2_2_read_weekend.helpMemoryIntro: The whole module in one story: 了 for completed actions, 过 for experiences, 没…过 for the ones still missing.

helpMemoryTips.title: Three stamps, one story
helpMemoryTips.text: 买了 (done), 没吃过 (experience missing), 还没去过 (still not yet). Find each in the text and say why it's not the others.

en_zh_a2_2_read_weekend.readingPassage: 上个周末汤姆很忙。星期六早上他去了商店，买了一件衬衫和一双鞋。下午他和小美去饭馆吃了北京烤鸭。汤姆以前没吃过烤鸭，他觉得太好吃了！星期天他在家学习中文，晚上给妈妈打了电话。妈妈问："你去过长城吗？"汤姆说："还没去过，我下个月想去。"
en_zh_a2_2_read_weekend.readingPassageTranslation:
Shàng ge zhōumò Tāngmǔ hěn máng. Xīngqīliù zǎoshang tā qù le shāngdiàn, mǎi le yí jiàn chènshān hé yì shuāng xié. Xiàwǔ tā hé Xiǎoměi qù fànguǎn chī le Běijīng kǎoyā. Tāngmǔ yǐqián méi chī guo kǎoyā, tā juéde tài hǎochī le! Xīngqītiān tā zài jiā xuéxí Zhōngwén, wǎnshang gěi māma dǎ le diànhuà. Māma wèn: "Nǐ qù guo Chángchéng ma?" Tāngmǔ shuō: "Hái méi qù guo, wǒ xià ge yuè xiǎng qù."

Last weekend Tom was busy. On Saturday morning he went to the shops and bought a shirt and a pair of shoes. In the afternoon he and Xiaomei ate Peking duck at a restaurant. Tom had never had roast duck before — he thought it was delicious! On Sunday he studied Chinese at home, and in the evening he phoned his mum. Mum asked: "Have you been to the Great Wall?" Tom said: "Not yet — I'd like to go next month."

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Had Tom eaten roast duck before?

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When would Tom like to go to the Great Wall?

en_zh_a2_2_shopping.helpMemoryIntro: Money talk: 多少钱? how much? Prices come in 块 kuài (yuan) and 毛 máo (tenths). Too expensive? 太贵了!

helpMemoryTips.title: 太…了 = way too …
helpMemoryTips.text: 太贵了! too expensive! 太好了! great! The 太…了 sandwich turns any adjective up to eleven.

helpMemoryTips.title: 块 on the street, 元 on the receipt
helpMemoryTips.text: Spoken prices use 块 (and 毛 for tenths); written prices use 元/角. 二十五块五 = ¥25.50.

en_zh_a2_2_speak_bu_yi.title: Sounds: 不 & 一 change tone

subjects.english: bú shì, bú qù, bú lèi — 不 before 4th tones

Wǒ bú shì lǎoshī. — I'm not a teacher.

subjects.display: 我买了一件衬衫和一双鞋。
subjects.english: Wǒ mǎi le yí jiàn chènshān hé yì shuāng xié. — I bought a shirt and a pair of shoes.

en_zh_a2_2_speak_bu_yi.helpMemoryIntro: Two everyday words bend their tone: 不 bù → bú before a 4th tone, and 一 yī → yí before a 4th, yì before the rest. Say them until it's automatic.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 不 flips before a fall (Z2)
helpMemoryTips.text: bù + 4th → bú: 不是 bú shì, 不去 bú qù, 不累 bú lèi. Everywhere else it stays bù: 不高, 不忙, 不喝.

helpMemoryTips.title: 一 has three faces
helpMemoryTips.text: Counting: yī (一, 十一). Before a 4th tone: yí (一件, 一个*). Before tones 1/2/3: yì (一杯, 一瓶, 一本). *个 counts as 4th.

en_zh_b1_1_bigtext_de.title: Big text: 的/得/地 in a letter
en_zh_b1_1_bigtext_de.helpMemoryIntro: Tom's letter home — with every de removed. Read it once, then choose 的, 得 or 地 for each gap: what does the de touch?

helpMemoryTips.title: The three-question test (Z20)
helpMemoryTips.text: Before a noun? → 的. After a verb, grading how it went? → 得. Before a verb, styling how it's done? → 地. Every gap answers one of the three.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ noun-的 · how-it-went-得 · how-you-do-it-地 (Z20)

helpMemoryTips.title: One frame, three de
helpMemoryTips.text: 他是很好的老师 · 他教得很好 · 他认真地教 — same teacher, three different de.

helpMemoryTips.title: The speaker is the compass (Z21)

helpMemoryTips.title: Places squeeze in the middle

en_zh_b1_1_duration.helpMemoryIntro: When something happens goes BEFORE the verb; how long it lasts goes AFTER: 我学了三年中文 — I studied Chinese for three years.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ WHEN before, HOW-LONG after (Z13)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我昨天(when)睡了十个小时(how long). Point in time = scene-setting → front. Amount of time = result-like → after the verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Still going on? Double 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我学了三年了 — the second 了 says the three years reach into now: "…and counting". One 了 = a closed chapter.

en_zh_b1_1_health.helpMemoryIntro: Aches, colds and the doctor. The pattern for pain: body part + 疼 — 我头疼, literally "I head-hurt".

helpMemoryTips.title: X 疼 = my X hurts
helpMemoryTips.text: 头疼 headache, 肚子疼 stomach ache — no "have a" needed: the body part is the topic and 疼 does the rest (Z28 preview).

en_zh_b1_1_listen_advice.title: Listening: 王老师的建议
en_zh_b1_1_listen_advice.helpMemoryIntro: Teacher Wang's three tips — a listening full of landings (学好, 说错, 写完, 写对) and both de-graders.

helpMemoryTips.title: 第 makes ordinals
helpMemoryTips.text: 第一, 第二, 第三 — first, second, third. 第 + number turns any count into a ranking.

en_zh_b1_1_listen_advice.readingPassage: 很多学生问我，怎么才能学好中文。我想说三件事。第一，每天都要听，听得越多，懂得越多。第二，别怕说错。说错了没关系，说得多了，就说得好了。第三，认真地写汉字。写完一个字，要问自己：我写对了吗？因为学外语不容易，所以要慢慢来。
en_zh_b1_1_listen_advice.readingPassageTranslation:
Hěn duō xuésheng wèn wǒ, zěnme cái néng xué hǎo Zhōngwén. Wǒ xiǎng shuō sān jiàn shì. Dì yī, měitiān dōu yào tīng, tīng de yuè duō, dǒng de yuè duō. Dì èr, bié pà shuō cuò. Shuō cuò le méi guānxi, shuō de duō le, jiù shuō de hǎo le. Dì sān, rènzhēn de xiě Hànzì. Xiě wán yí ge zì, yào wèn zìjǐ: wǒ xiě duì le ma? Yīnwèi xué wàiyǔ bù róngyì, suǒyǐ yào mànmàn lái.

Many students ask me how to master Chinese. I'd say three things. First, listen every day — the more you hear, the more you understand. Second, don't fear mistakes. Misspeaking doesn't matter: speak a lot and you'll speak well. Third, write characters carefully. When you finish one, ask yourself: did I write it right? Learning a language isn't easy, so take it step by step.

readingQuestions.question: 王老师说了几件事？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How many points does Teacher Wang make?

readingQuestions.question: 说错了怎么办？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What about making mistakes when speaking?

readingQuestions.question: 写完一个字，要问自己什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: After finishing a character, what should you ask yourself?

en_zh_b1_1_listen_hospital.title: Listening: 去医院
en_zh_b1_1_listen_hospital.helpMemoryIntro: Tom gets sick. Listen for the landings — 听懂了, 好点儿了, 好多了 — they carry the story's progress.

helpMemoryTips.title: 好点儿了 / 好多了
helpMemoryTips.text: Recovery in two sizes: 好(一)点儿了 a bit better, 好多了 much better — comparison + change-了 in one phrase.

en_zh_b1_1_listen_hospital.readingPassage: 汤姆早上起床的时候，觉得头很疼。他没去上课，去了医院。医生看了看，说："你感冒了。回家好好休息，多喝水，吃这个药。"汤姆听懂了医生的话，买了药就回家了。下午小美打电话问他："你好点儿了吗？"汤姆说："好多了，谢谢！"
en_zh_b1_1_listen_hospital.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ zǎoshang qǐchuáng de shíhou, juéde tóu hěn téng. Tā méi qù shàngkè, qù le yīyuàn. Yīshēng kàn le kàn, shuō: "Nǐ gǎnmào le. Huí jiā hǎohāo xiūxi, duō hē shuǐ, chī zhè ge yào." Tāngmǔ tīng dǒng le yīshēng de huà, mǎi le yào jiù huí jiā le. Xiàwǔ Xiǎoměi dǎ diànhuà wèn tā: "Nǐ hǎo diǎnr le ma?" Tāngmǔ shuō: "Hǎo duō le, xièxie!"

When Tom got up in the morning, his head hurt. He didn't go to class — he went to the hospital. The doctor had a look and said: "You've caught a cold. Go home and rest properly, drink lots of water, take this medicine." Tom understood the doctor, bought the medicine and went straight home. In the afternoon Xiaomei phoned to ask: "Are you feeling a bit better?" Tom said: "Much better, thanks!"

readingQuestions.question: 医生让汤姆做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does the doctor tell Tom to do?

readingQuestions.question: 下午汤姆怎么样了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How is Tom in the afternoon?

en_zh_b1_1_pairs.helpMemoryIntro: Chinese connectives come in pairs and keep both halves: 因为 A，所以 B (because A, so B); 虽然 A，但是 B (although A, but B).

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't drop the second half (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: English "although" bans a following "but" — Chinese REQUIRES it: 虽然贵，**但是**很好. Dropping 但是/所以 sounds broken, not elegant.

en_zh_b1_1_read_learning.title: Reading: 学中文的路
en_zh_b1_1_read_learning.helpMemoryIntro: Tom's first year — told with this module's whole toolkit: duration, landings, the three de, and one tone slip that proves why tones matter.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ wèn ≠ wěn
helpMemoryTips.text: 问 (ask, 4th tone) vs 吻 (kiss, 3rd tone) — the passage's joke is a real cautionary tale about tones (Z1).

en_zh_b1_1_read_learning.readingPassage: 汤姆学中文学了一年了。开始的时候，他觉得声调太难了，常常说错。有一次，他想说"我想问你"，可是说成了"我想吻你"，大家都笑了。现在他听得懂老师说的话，也看得懂简单的中文书。他每天认真地学习，写字写得越来越漂亮。王老师说："学外语就是这样：慢慢来，别怕说错。"汤姆觉得，虽然中文很难，但是他学得很开心。
en_zh_b1_1_read_learning.readingPassageTranslation:
Tāngmǔ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le. Kāishǐ de shíhou, tā juéde shēngdiào tài nán le, chángcháng shuō cuò. Yǒu yí cì, tā xiǎng shuō "wǒ xiǎng wèn nǐ", kěshì shuō chéng le "wǒ xiǎng wěn nǐ", dàjiā dōu xiào le. Xiànzài tā tīng de dǒng lǎoshī shuō de huà, yě kàn de dǒng jiǎndān de Zhōngwén shū. Tā měitiān rènzhēn de xuéxí, xiě zì xiě de yuèláiyuè piàoliang. Wáng lǎoshī shuō: "Xué wàiyǔ jiù shì zhèyàng: mànmàn lái, bié pà shuō cuò." Tāngmǔ juéde, suīrán Zhōngwén hěn nán, dànshì tā xué de hěn kāixīn.

Tom has been learning Chinese for a year now. At the beginning he found the tones too hard and often misspoke. Once he meant to say "I want to ask you" (wèn) but said "I want to kiss you" (wěn) — everyone laughed. Now he can understand what the teacher says and read simple Chinese books. He studies conscientiously every day, and his characters look better and better. Teacher Wang says: "That's what learning a language is: take it slowly, don't fear mistakes." Tom feels that although Chinese is hard, he's learning it very happily.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆学中文学了多长时间了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How long has Tom been learning Chinese?

readingQuestions.question: 开始的时候，汤姆觉得什么太难了？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Tom find too hard at the beginning?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆想说"问"，说成了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Tom meant to say "ask" — what did he say instead?

en_zh_b1_1_read_sick.title: Reading: 汤姆病了
en_zh_b1_1_read_sick.helpMemoryIntro: The whole module in a story: durations (两天, 十二个小时), landings (买来), pairs (因为…所以) and a graded 得 (好得这么快).

helpMemoryTips.title: 买来 = bought & brought
helpMemoryTips.text: 买来了药 — the 来 lands the buying at Tom's door. Directional complements sneak onto ordinary verbs everywhere (Z21).

en_zh_b1_1_read_sick.readingPassage: 上个星期，汤姆病了。他头疼，肚子也疼，两天没去上课。小美给他买来了药和水果。她说："多休息，多喝水，你很快就会好的。"汤姆吃了药，睡了十二个小时。第二天，他觉得好多了。他给小美打电话："谢谢你！因为你的帮助，所以我好得这么快。"小美笑着说："别客气！朋友就是要互相帮助。"
en_zh_b1_1_read_sick.readingPassageTranslation:
Shàng ge xīngqī, Tāngmǔ bìng le. Tā tóu téng, dùzi yě téng, liǎng tiān méi qù shàngkè. Xiǎoměi gěi tā mǎi lái le yào hé shuǐguǒ. Tā shuō: "Duō xiūxi, duō hē shuǐ, nǐ hěn kuài jiù huì hǎo de." Tāngmǔ chī le yào, shuì le shí'èr ge xiǎoshí. Dì èr tiān, tā juéde hǎo duō le. Tā gěi Xiǎoměi dǎ diànhuà: "Xièxie nǐ! Yīnwèi nǐ de bāngzhù, suǒyǐ wǒ hǎo de zhème kuài." Xiǎoměi xiào zhe shuō: "Bié kèqi! Péngyou jiù shì yào hùxiāng bāngzhù."

Last week Tom fell ill. His head hurt, his stomach too, and he missed class for two days. Xiaomei bought him medicine and fruit. She said: "Rest a lot, drink lots of water — you'll be better in no time." Tom took the medicine and slept twelve hours. The next day he felt much better. He phoned Xiaomei: "Thank you! It's thanks to your help that I got better so fast." Xiaomei said with a smile: "Don't mention it! Friends are there to help each other."

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆几天没去上课？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How many days did Tom miss class?

readingQuestions.question: 小美给汤姆买来了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did Xiaomei buy and bring Tom?

en_zh_b1_1_result_1.helpMemoryIntro: 找 is to look — 找到 is to find. Chinese verbs describe the attempt; a result complement lands them: 完 finished, 到 attained, 懂 understood.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Verb + landing (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: English packs result into the verb (find, hear); Chinese splits it: 找 look + 到 = find; 听 listen + 懂 = understand (by ear); 吃 eat + 完 = finish eating.

helpMemoryTips.title: The landing takes the 了
helpMemoryTips.text: 我看完了这本书 — the ✓-stamp follows the whole verb+landing unit: 看完了, 找到了, 听懂了.

en_zh_b1_1_result_2.helpMemoryIntro: 见 registers perception (看见 see, 听见 hear), 好 means done-and-ready, 错 means wrongly. Negate a missed result with 没: 我没听懂.

helpMemoryTips.title: 没 + verb + landing (Z21/Z17)
helpMemoryTips.text: The result didn't happen → 没, and the 了 goes: 我没看见他 I didn't see him; 我还没做完 I'm not done yet.

helpMemoryTips.title: 错 = did it, but wrongly
helpMemoryTips.text: 我说错了 I misspoke; 你打错了 wrong number. The action happened — the landing says it went wrong.

en_zh_b1_1_speak_results.title: Speaking: verb + landing drills

subjects.english: Wǒ zhǎo dào le! — I found it!

Duìbuqǐ, wǒ shuō cuò le. — Sorry, I said it wrong.
Nǐ kàn jiàn wǒ de yàoshi le ma? — Have you seen my keys?

en_zh_b1_1_speak_results.helpMemoryIntro: Drill the verb-landing pairs aloud until they feel like single words — because to a Chinese ear, they are.

helpMemoryTips.title: Stress the landing
helpMemoryTips.text: The complement carries the news: 找到了! (FOUND it), 听懂了! (GOT it). Let your voice land on the landing (Z21).

en_zh_b1_1_speak_rhythm.title: Speaking: longer sentences, steady tones

subjects.english: Wǒ xué Zhōngwén xué le yì nián le. — I've been learning Chinese for a year.
Tā shuō Zhōngwén shuō de fēicháng hǎo. — She speaks Chinese extremely well.

subjects.display: 因为我病了，所以没去上课。
subjects.english: Yīnwèi wǒ bìng le, suǒyǐ méi qù shàngkè. — Because I was ill, I didn't go to class.

subjects.display: 请你慢慢地说，我听得懂。
subjects.english: Qǐng nǐ mànmàn de shuō, wǒ tīng de dǒng. — Speak slowly please, and I can understand.

subjects.display: 虽然很难，但是很有意思。
subjects.english: Suīrán hěn nán, dànshì hěn yǒuyìsi. — Hard, but interesting.

en_zh_b1_1_speak_rhythm.helpMemoryIntro: Longer sentences now — keep every syllable's tone while the sentence flows. Chinese rhythm gives each syllable its beat.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't stress-time it (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: English squeezes unstressed syllables; Chinese gives each syllable even weight. Resist rushing the "small" words — 了, 的, 得 stay clear (just lighter).

en_zh_b1_2_dict_describe.title: Dictation: descriptions

subjects.english: The book I bought is very interesting.
It was in Beijing that she learned Chinese.

en_zh_b1_2_dict_describe.helpMemoryIntro: Type what you hear — 的-clauses, 是…的 spotlights and potential complements included.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Hear the clause seam
helpMemoryTips.text: In 我昨天买的书, the tiny 的 splits clause from noun. Miss it and the IME will offer you nonsense — the seam is the meaning (Z19).

en_zh_b1_2_listen_shide.title: Listening: 他是什么时候来的?
en_zh_b1_2_listen_shide.helpMemoryIntro: Every answer in this dialogue is a 是…的 spotlight: when, from where, how, with whom. Catch each detail.

helpMemoryTips.title: 从…来 = come from
helpMemoryTips.text: 从 (from) is a coverb: 从加拿大来 — from-Canada come. Another scene-setter that stands before the verb (Z29).

en_zh_b1_2_listen_shide.readingPassage:
小美："我们班有一个新同学，你见过他吗？"
汤姆："见过。他是上个月来的。"
小美："他是从哪儿来的？"
汤姆："他是从加拿大来的，是坐飞机来的。"
小美："他的中文说得怎么样？"
汤姆："说得非常好！他是在家跟妈妈学的——他妈妈是中国人。"
en_zh_b1_2_listen_shide.readingPassageTranslation:
Xiǎoměi: "Wǒmen bān yǒu yí ge xīn tóngxué, nǐ jiàn guo tā ma?"
Tāngmǔ: "Jiàn guo. Tā shì shàng ge yuè lái de."
Xiǎoměi: "Tā shì cóng nǎr lái de?"
Tāngmǔ: "Tā shì cóng Jiānádà lái de, shì zuò fēijī lái de."
Xiǎoměi: "Tā de Zhōngwén shuō de zěnmeyàng?"
Tāngmǔ: "Shuō de fēicháng hǎo! Tā shì zài jiā gēn māma xué de — tā māma shì Zhōngguó rén."

Xiaomei: "There's a new classmate in our class — have you met him?"
Tom: "I have. He came last month."
Xiaomei: "Where is he from?"
Tom: "He's from Canada — he came by plane."
Xiaomei: "How's his Chinese?"
Tom: "Excellent! He learned it at home with his mum — his mum is Chinese."

readingQuestions.question: 新同学是什么时候来的？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When did the new classmate come?

readingQuestions.question: 他的中文是跟谁学的？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who did he learn Chinese with?

en_zh_b1_2_listen_weather.title: Listening: 天气预报
en_zh_b1_2_listen_weather.helpMemoryIntro: A weather forecast for four cities. Listen for city + weather + temperature — and one 比-comparison.

helpMemoryTips.title: 度 = degrees, 零下 = below zero
helpMemoryTips.text: 二十八度 28°, 零下十度 −10°. The 比-line: 比今天热三度 — hotter than today BY three degrees (the amount follows the adjective, Z24).

en_zh_b1_2_listen_weather.readingPassage: 大家好，现在播报明天的天气。北京明天是晴天，不刮风，白天二十八度，是个又暖和又舒服的日子。上海明天上午有小雨，下午雨就停了，二十五度。广州明天天气很热，三十四度，比今天热三度。哈尔滨的朋友要注意：明天下大雪，零下十度，出门的时候要多穿衣服。
en_zh_b1_2_listen_weather.readingPassageTranslation:
Dàjiā hǎo, xiànzài bōbào míngtiān de tiānqì. Běijīng míngtiān shì qíngtiān, bù guā fēng, báitiān èrshíbā dù, shì ge yòu nuǎnhuo yòu shūfu de rìzi. Shànghǎi míngtiān shàngwǔ yǒu xiǎo yǔ, xiàwǔ yǔ jiù tíng le, èrshíwǔ dù. Guǎngzhōu míngtiān tiānqì hěn rè, sānshísì dù, bǐ jīntiān rè sān dù. Hā'ěrbīn de péngyou yào zhùyì: míngtiān xià dà xuě, língxià shí dù, chūmén de shíhou yào duō chuān yīfu.

Hello everyone, here is tomorrow's weather. Beijing: sunny, no wind, 28 degrees in the day — a warm, comfortable day. Shanghai: light rain in the morning, stopping by afternoon, 25 degrees. Guangzhou: very hot, 34 degrees — three degrees hotter than today. Friends in Harbin, take note: heavy snow tomorrow, minus ten — dress warmly when you go out.

readingQuestions.question: 北京明天天气怎么样？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What is tomorrow's weather in Beijing?

readingQuestions.question: 上海的雨什么时候停？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When does the rain in Shanghai stop?

readingQuestions.question: 哪个城市明天下大雪？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Which city gets heavy snow tomorrow?

en_zh_b1_2_potential.helpMemoryIntro: Slide 得 or 不 between verb and landing to say whether the result is reachable: 听得懂 can understand, 听不懂 can't understand.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ The landing decides, 得/不 predicts (Z21)
helpMemoryTips.text: 看得完 can finish reading it, 看不完 can't possibly finish. This beats 能 for ability tied to a RESULT: 我听不懂 ≈ "it won't land in my ears".

helpMemoryTips.title: Questions pair both
helpMemoryTips.text: 你听得懂听不懂? or 你听得懂吗? — either asks "can you follow?"

en_zh_b1_2_read_people.title: Reading: 我认识的人
en_zh_b1_2_read_people.helpMemoryIntro: Four people, each introduced by a 的-clause. Parse each: find the 的, find the noun, then read the description before it.

helpMemoryTips.title: Chunk, don't crawl (Z8)
helpMemoryTips.text: 住在他楼上的|老爷爷 — split at the 的. Reading Chinese means grouping characters into words and clauses; the 的 is your best seam.

en_zh_b1_2_read_people.readingPassage: 在北京，汤姆认识了很多有意思的人。住在他楼上的老爷爷每天早上在公园里打太极拳，他是三十年前从上海来的。在咖啡馆工作的那个女孩儿会说四种语言，她说得又快又好。教汤姆写汉字的王老师写的字漂亮得像画儿一样。汤姆觉得，认识的人越多，他的中文就越好，生活也越来越有意思。
en_zh_b1_2_read_people.readingPassageTranslation:
Zài Běijīng, Tāngmǔ rènshi le hěn duō yǒuyìsi de rén. Zhù zài tā lóushàng de lǎo yéye měitiān zǎoshang zài gōngyuán li dǎ tàijíquán, tā shì sānshí nián qián cóng Shànghǎi lái de. Zài kāfēiguǎn gōngzuò de nà ge nǚháir huì shuō sì zhǒng yǔyán, tā shuō de yòu kuài yòu hǎo. Jiāo Tāngmǔ xiě Hànzì de Wáng lǎoshī xiě de zì piàoliang de xiàng huàr yíyàng. Tāngmǔ juéde, rènshi de rén yuè duō, tā de Zhōngwén jiù yuè hǎo, shēnghuó yě yuèláiyuè yǒuyìsi.

In Beijing, Tom has gotten to know many interesting people. The old grandpa who lives upstairs does tai chi in the park every morning — he came from Shanghai thirty years ago. The girl who works at the café speaks four languages, fast and well. Teacher Wang, who teaches Tom to write characters, writes characters as beautiful as paintings. Tom finds that the more people he knows, the better his Chinese gets — and life keeps getting more interesting.

readingQuestions.question: 住在楼上的老爷爷是从哪儿来的？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Where did the grandpa upstairs come from?

readingQuestions.question: 谁会说四种语言？
options: 在咖啡馆工作的女孩儿

readingQuestions.question: 王老师教汤姆什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Teacher Wang teach Tom?

en_zh_b1_2_read_seasons.title: Reading: 北京的四季
en_zh_b1_2_read_seasons.helpMemoryIntro: Four seasons, packed with this module's frames: 又…又, 越来越, 的-clauses and a closing 如果…就.

helpMemoryTips.title: 最 = the most
helpMemoryTips.text: 最热 hottest, 最漂亮 most beautiful, 最喜欢 favourite — 最 simply fronts the adjective. No "-est" forms to build.

en_zh_b1_2_read_seasons.readingPassage: 北京的四季很不一样。春天暖和，可是常常刮风。夏天又热又长，最热的时候有三十八度，白天出门的人都走得很快，因为大家都想快点儿回到凉快的家里。秋天是北京最漂亮的季节：天很蓝，路两边的树越来越黄，来公园拍照片的人也越来越多。冬天很冷，有时候下大雪。下雪的时候，孩子们玩得最高兴。汤姆最喜欢的季节是秋天。他说："如果你秋天来北京，就会爱上这个城市。"
en_zh_b1_2_read_seasons.readingPassageTranslation:
Běijīng de sìjì hěn bù yíyàng. Chūntiān nuǎnhuo, kěshì chángcháng guā fēng. Xiàtiān yòu rè yòu cháng, zuì rè de shíhou yǒu sānshíbā dù, báitiān chūmén de rén dōu zǒu de hěn kuài, yīnwèi dàjiā dōu xiǎng kuài diǎnr huí dào liángkuai de jiā li. Qiūtiān shì Běijīng zuì piàoliang de jìjié: tiān hěn lán, lù liǎngbiān de shù yuèláiyuè huáng, lái gōngyuán pāi zhàopiàn de rén yě yuèláiyuè duō. Dōngtiān hěn lěng, yǒushíhou xià dà xuě. Xià xuě de shíhou, háizimen wán de zuì gāoxìng. Tāngmǔ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié shì qiūtiān. Tā shuō: "Rúguǒ nǐ qiūtiān lái Běijīng, jiù huì àishàng zhè ge chéngshì."

Beijing's four seasons are very different. Spring is warm but often windy. Summer is hot and long — at its hottest it reaches 38 degrees, and people out in the daytime walk fast, because everyone wants to get back to a cool home. Autumn is Beijing's most beautiful season: the sky is blue, the trees along the roads turn more and more yellow, and more and more people come to the parks to take photos. Winter is cold, sometimes with heavy snow. When it snows, the children have the best time. Tom's favourite season is autumn. He says: "If you come to Beijing in autumn, you'll fall in love with this city."

readingQuestions.question: 北京哪个季节最漂亮？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Which is Beijing's most beautiful season?

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: How hot does it get at the height of summer?

readingQuestions.question: 下雪的时候，谁玩得最高兴？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who has the most fun when it snows?

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Description first, noun last (Z19)
helpMemoryTips.text: English: noun + that-clause. Chinese: clause + 的 + noun. 喝咖啡的人 = the person who's drinking coffee — read up to 的, then meet the noun.

helpMemoryTips.title: No who/which/that
helpMemoryTips.text: Chinese has no relative pronoun at all: the 的 does everything. 我认识的老师 — the teacher (whom) I know.

en_zh_b1_2_ruguo.helpMemoryIntro: 如果 A，B 就… — if A, then B. The 就 sits inside the second clause, right before its verb: 如果下雨，我们就不去.

helpMemoryTips.title: Another pair to keep (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 如果 opens the condition, 就 answers it. 就 is an adverb: it must stand before the verb, never before the subject — 就我们不去 ✗.

helpMemoryTips.title: No tense gymnastics
helpMemoryTips.text: English shifts tenses ("if it rains… we would…"); Chinese conditions stay bare: 如果…就 handles real and hypothetical alike (Z9).

en_zh_b1_2_shi_de.helpMemoryIntro: For past events, 是…的 spotlights when/where/how: 我是昨天来的 — it was YESTERDAY that I came. The event is known; the detail is the news.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Known event, new detail (Z28)
helpMemoryTips.text: Use 是…的 when the happening is old news and you're asking or telling the circumstance: 你是怎么来的? (HOW did you come?) — not plain 了, which reports the event itself.

helpMemoryTips.title: The frame
helpMemoryTips.text: 是 + [spotlighted detail + verb] + 的: 她是在北京学的中文, 我们是坐飞机来的.

en_zh_b2_1_ba_1.helpMemoryIntro: To say what you DID to something, grab it first: 我把门关上了 — I took the door and shut it. 把 + object + verb + landing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Grab it, then do it (Z22)
helpMemoryTips.text: S + 把 + object + verb + RESULT. The verb can't stand bare: 把门关 ✗ — it needs a landing (关上, 吃完, 放在…). 把 fronts the object so the action's effect takes the spotlight.

helpMemoryTips.title: When to reach for 把
helpMemoryTips.text: Known, specific object + what happened to it → 把. Telling someone what to do with things (put, move, finish, close) practically demands it.

helpMemoryTips.title: Victim + 被 + (culprit) + verb + landing (Z23)

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't translate every English passive with 被
helpMemoryTips.text: "The problem was solved" is NOT 被: say 问题解决了 (next quiz). 被 fits mishaps and formal reports — overusing it is textbook foreign accent.

en_zh_b2_1_listen_cake.helpMemoryIntro: A missing-cake mystery, told in 把 and 被. (From now on the info button is English-only — your pinyin training wheels are off.)

helpMemoryTips.title: 把 accuses, 被 defends
helpMemoryTips.text: 谁把蛋糕吃了? points at a doer; 蛋糕没被人吃 clears everyone. The same event, grabbed from both ends (Z22/Z23).

en_zh_b2_1_listen_cake.readingPassage:
晚上，小美回到家，打开冰箱，发现她的生日蛋糕不见了。
小美："谁把我的蛋糕吃了？！"
弟弟："不是我！我下午一直在踢足球。"
爸爸："我也没吃。你去问问你妈妈。"
妈妈笑了："蛋糕没被人吃，我把它放到楼上了，因为今天晚上我们要给你一个惊喜。生日快乐！"
en_zh_b2_1_listen_cake.readingPassageTranslation:
In the evening, Xiaomei comes home, opens the fridge, and finds her birthday cake gone.
Xiaomei: "Who ate my cake?!"
Little brother: "Not me! I was playing football all afternoon."
Dad: "I didn't eat it either. Go ask your mum."
Mum laughs: "Nobody ate the cake — I moved it upstairs, because tonight we're giving you a surprise. Happy birthday!"

helpMemoryTips.text: 您 nín is 你 with a heart (心) underneath — the respectful "you" for bosses, elders and customers. 谢谢您!

en_zh_b2_1_listen_interview.readingPassage:
汤姆想找一份兼职工作，今天他去一家翻译公司面试。
经理："你为什么想来我们公司工作？"
汤姆："因为我喜欢语言。我会说英文和法文，中文也说得越来越好。"
经理："你能把这段中文翻译成英文吗？"
汤姆看了看，把那段话翻译了出来。
经理很满意："翻译得不错！下星期一你能来上班吗？"
汤姆高兴地说："能！谢谢您给我这个机会。"
en_zh_b2_1_listen_interview.readingPassageTranslation:
Tom wants a part-time job, and today he has an interview at a translation company.
Manager: "Why do you want to work at our company?"
Tom: "Because I love languages. I speak English and French, and my Chinese keeps getting better."
Manager: "Can you translate this Chinese passage into English?"
Tom looks it over and translates the passage.
The manager is pleased: "Nicely translated! Can you start next Monday?"
Tom says happily: "I can! Thank you for giving me this opportunity."

readingQuestions.question: 经理让汤姆做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does the manager have Tom do?

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆什么时候开始上班？

helpMemoryTips.title: A + 让 + B + verb
helpMemoryTips.text: The second verb belongs to B: 老板让我们加班 the boss makes us work late; 别让我等 don't make me wait. English "make/let/have someone do" collapses into 让.

en_zh_b2_1_read_delivery.title: Reading: 中国的快递
en_zh_b2_1_read_delivery.helpMemoryIntro: A slice of modern China — full of this module's grammar: 把, 被, comparisons and a 让 at the end.

helpMemoryTips.title: 被 without a culprit
helpMemoryTips.text: 能被送到家门口 / 能被再次使用 — formal-neutral 被 with no agent is fine in written style. Speech would just say 送到家门口 (Z23).

en_zh_b2_1_read_delivery.readingPassage:
在中国生活了一年以后，汤姆觉得最方便的就是快递。你在手机上买的东西，第二天就能被送到家门口。快递员每天把成千上万个包裹送到城市的每一个角落，比很多国家的快递快得多，也便宜得多。
上个星期，汤姆把一本书寄给在上海的朋友。他早上把书交给快递员，朋友第二天中午就收到了。朋友给他发消息："收到了！这也太快了吧！"
不过快递也带来了新问题：人们买得越来越多，包装垃圾也越来越多。现在很多公司开始让顾客把纸箱留给快递员，这样纸箱就能被再次使用。
en_zh_b2_1_read_delivery.readingPassageTranslation:
After a year of living in China, Tom thinks the most convenient thing of all is the express delivery system. Something you buy on your phone can be delivered to your door the next day. Couriers deliver tens of thousands of parcels to every corner of the city every day — much faster and much cheaper than in many countries.
Last week, Tom mailed a book to a friend in Shanghai. He handed the book to the courier in the morning, and his friend received it the next day at noon. The friend messaged him: "Got it! That's just too fast!"
But delivery brings new problems too: people buy more and more, and packaging waste keeps growing. Many companies now have customers leave the boxes with the courier, so the boxes can be used again.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆觉得在中国生活最方便的是什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom find most convenient about life in China?

readingQuestions.question: 朋友什么时候收到了书？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: When did the friend receive the book?

readingQuestions.question: 快递带来了什么新问题？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What new problem does delivery bring?

en_zh_b2_1_read_moving.title: Reading: 搬家
en_zh_b2_1_read_moving.helpMemoryIntro: Moving day: instructions with 把, one 被 for flavour, and comparisons between old home and new.

helpMemoryTips.title: 离 = distance from (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 新家离学校更近 — 离 measures the gap between two places: A 离 B 近/远. It's a coverb: it stands before what it relates to.

en_zh_b2_1_read_moving.readingPassage:
这个周末汤姆搬家了。新家比旧家大得多，离学校也更近。
小美和几个朋友都来帮忙。汤姆让大家先把大东西搬上车：床、桌子、椅子，还有那个最重的书柜。
"把书柜放在哪儿？"小美问。
"放在窗户旁边吧，"汤姆说，"把书都放到书柜里，把衣服放在床上，我等一下自己收拾。"
搬完家，大家都累了。汤姆把大家的水杯拿来，说："今天真是太感谢你们了！晚上我请大家吃饭——菜已经被我订好了！"
en_zh_b2_1_read_moving.readingPassageTranslation:
This weekend Tom moved house. The new place is much bigger than the old one, and closer to school too.
Xiaomei and a few friends came to help. Tom had everyone move the big things onto the truck first: the bed, the table, the chairs, and that heaviest of bookcases.
"Where do we put the bookcase?" Xiaomei asked.
"Next to the window," said Tom. "Put the books in the bookcase and the clothes on the bed — I'll sort them out myself later."
When the move was done, everyone was exhausted. Tom brought everyone's water and said: "Thank you all so much for today! Dinner's on me tonight — the food is already ordered!"

readingQuestions.question: 新家怎么样？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What is the new home like?

readingQuestions.question: 晚上谁请大家吃饭？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Who treats everyone to dinner in the evening?

en_zh_b2_1_speak_ba.title: Speaking: instructions with 把

subjects.english: Bǎ zhuōzi bān dào kètīng. — Move the table into the living room.
Qǐng bǎ mén guān shàng. — Please shut the door.
Bǎ yīfu fàng zài chuáng shàng ba. — Put the clothes on the bed.
Bié bǎ yàoshi wàng zài jiā li! — Don't leave the keys at home!
Bǎ zhè bēi chá ná gěi nǎinai. — Take this cup of tea to grandma.

en_zh_b2_1_speak_ba.helpMemoryIntro: Give instructions aloud — moving-day orders are pure 把 territory: grab the thing, say where it goes.

helpMemoryTips.title: Rhythm: 把-X | V-landing
helpMemoryTips.text: Chunk each order in two: 把桌子 | 搬到客厅. The pause after the object keeps long instructions clear (Z22).

en_zh_b2_1_speak_intonation.title: Speaking: question intonation OVER tones

subjects.english: Nǐ qù ma? — Are you going? (去 still falls!)
Nǐ shì shéi? — Who are you? (statement melody)
Nǐ bǎ yàoshi fàng zài nǎr le? — Where did you put the keys?
Zhè ge duōshao qián? — How much is this? (calm, no English rise)
Nǐ tīng de dǒng tīng bu dǒng? — Can you follow or not?

en_zh_b2_1_speak_intonation.helpMemoryIntro: A Chinese question rises as a whole — but every syllable keeps its own tone. Don't let English question-melody bend the words.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ The sentence rises, the tones survive (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: In 你去吗? the overall pitch floats up, but 去 still FALLS (4th tone) inside that float. English speakers turn 去 into a rise — and say a different word.

en_zh_b2_1_work.helpMemoryIntro: The vocabulary of jobs and offices — where 把-instructions and polite 让-requests live all day.

helpMemoryTips.title: 班 = your shift
helpMemoryTips.text: 上班 go on shift (start work), 下班 come off shift, 加班 add shift (overtime) — one noun, three daily verbs.

en_zh_b2_2_bigtext_aspect.title: Big text: 了 / 过 / 着 — the aspect story
en_zh_b2_2_bigtext_aspect.helpMemoryIntro: One Saturday, ten gaps, three particles. For each: completed and counted → 了; life experience → 过; held state or backdrop → 着.

helpMemoryTips.title: The three stamps side by side (Z14/Z15/Z16)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了 = ✓ done · 过 = passport-stamped experience · 着 = pause button. If the sentence counts something (一杯, 二十分钟), 了. If it says "ever/never", 过. If something just hangs there, 着.

en_zh_b2_2_bigtext_aspect.readingPassage:
星期六早上，汤姆睡到九点。窗户开着，外面下着小雨。
他喝了一杯咖啡，然后坐着看书。这本书他以前看过一遍，可是越看越喜欢。
中午，小美来电话："你吃饭了吗？我知道一家新饭馆，我还没去过，一起去吧！"
饭馆里人很多。他们等了二十分钟才坐下。墙上挂着很多老照片，菜也很好吃。汤姆笑着说："下个星期我们再来吧！"
en_zh_b2_2_bigtext_aspect.readingPassageTranslation: Saturday morning Tom sleeps till nine. The window stands open; outside a light rain is falling. He drinks a cup of coffee, then sits reading. He's read this book once before, but likes it more with every page. At noon Xiaomei calls: "Have you eaten? I know a new restaurant — I haven't been yet. Let's go together!" The restaurant is packed. They wait twenty minutes before getting a table. Old photos hang on the walls, and the food is great. Tom says with a smile: "Let's come again next week!"

en_zh_b2_2_dou_ye_hai.helpMemoryIntro: 都 all, 也 also, 还 still/in addition — small adverbs with a fixed home: after the subject, before the verb. 都 sums up what stands BEFORE it.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 都 points backward (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 我们都去 — ALL of us go: 都 covers the crowd to its LEFT. "I read all the books" = 这些书我都看过 — front the books so 都 can see them.

helpMemoryTips.title: Order in the slot: 也 > 都 > 还
helpMemoryTips.text: Stacked, they keep this order: 我们也都还在等 — also-all-still waiting. Each stays before the verb, never after.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 就 = sooner than you think, 才 = later than you'd like (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 就 says "that fast/easy/soon"; 才 says "only then, not before". Note: 才 blocks 了 — 他十点才来(了✗).

en_zh_b2_2_listen_podcast.title: Listening: 播客 — 好习惯
en_zh_b2_2_listen_podcast.helpMemoryIntro: A podcast on habits — listen for 只要…就 vs 只有…才 doing real argumentative work, plus 着, 即使…也 and 无论…都.

helpMemoryTips.title: 听起来 = it sounds…
helpMemoryTips.text: 听起来很简单 — "hearing-wise it comes out simple". The abstract 起来 turns any verb into an impression: 看起来, 说起来 (Z21).

en_zh_b2_2_listen_podcast.readingPassage:
大家好，欢迎收听我们的播客。今天聊一个话题：好习惯是怎么来的？
很多人觉得，只要下定决心，就能改变自己。可是研究发现，只有把新习惯变得很小、很容易，才能坚持下去。比如，你想每天看书，就先从每天看一页开始。即使那天再忙，一页书也看得完。
还有一个方法：把新习惯放在老习惯后面。每天喝着咖啡的时候背五个生词——咖啡喝完了，生词也背完了。听起来很简单吧？无论你想养成什么习惯，都可以试试这个办法。
en_zh_b2_2_listen_podcast.readingPassageTranslation:
Hello everyone, welcome to our podcast. Today's topic: where do good habits come from?
Many people think that as long as you're determined, you can change yourself. But research finds that only by making a new habit small and easy can you keep it going. Say you want to read every day — start with one page a day. Even on your busiest day, one page is doable.
Another method: attach the new habit to an old one. Memorize five new words while drinking your daily coffee — when the coffee's finished, so are the words. Sounds simple, right? Whatever habit you want to build, give this method a try.

readingQuestions.question: 研究发现，怎样才能坚持新习惯？
options: 把习惯变得很小、很容易
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: According to research, how can you keep a new habit going?

readingQuestions.question: 想每天看书，应该从什么开始？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: To read daily, what should you start with?

readingQuestions.question: 喝咖啡的时候可以做什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What can you do while drinking coffee?

en_zh_b2_2_listen_waiting.title: Listening: 等人
en_zh_b2_2_listen_waiting.helpMemoryIntro: One little story, all the little adverbs: 就 (early), 才 (finally), 又 (again!), 还 (still), plus a 着 and a 吧.

helpMemoryTips.title: 就要…了 = about to
helpMemoryTips.text: 电影就要开始了 — on the very edge of starting. 就 + 要 + verb + 了 is the "any second now" frame (Z27).

en_zh_b2_2_listen_waiting.readingPassage:
星期六下午两点，汤姆和小美约好在电影院门口见面，电影两点半开始。
汤姆一点半就到了，站着等小美。两点过了，小美还没来。他给小美发消息："你到哪儿了？电影就要开始了！"
两点二十五，小美才跑来，笑着说："对不起对不起！我又坐错车了！"
汤姆说："你上次也坐错了！快走吧，再不进去，电影就开始了！"
en_zh_b2_2_listen_waiting.readingPassageTranslation:
Saturday afternoon at two, Tom and Xiaomei have agreed to meet at the cinema entrance; the film starts at half past two.
Tom arrives at half past one already and stands there waiting. Two o'clock passes — still no Xiaomei. He messages her: "Where are you? The film is about to start!"
At 2:25 Xiaomei finally comes running, saying with a laugh: "Sorry, sorry! I took the wrong bus again!"
Tom says: "You took the wrong one last time too! Quick — if we don't go in now, the film will start!"

readingQuestions.question: 小美是第几次坐错车？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: Is this the first time Xiaomei took the wrong bus?

en_zh_b2_2_pairs.helpMemoryIntro: Three heavyweight pairs: 不但 A 而且 B (not only… but also), 只要 A 就 B (as long as → enough), 只有 A 才 B (only if → necessary).

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 只要…就 is generous, 只有…才 is strict (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 只要练习，就会进步 — ANY practice brings progress (sufficient). 只有练习，才会进步 — NOTHING BUT practice brings it (necessary). The closer (就 vs 才) matches the opener.

en_zh_b2_2_read_date.title: Reading: 一次约会
en_zh_b2_2_read_date.helpMemoryIntro: A first date told through the module's lens: 就 vs 才, 着-states, 不但…而且, 只有…才 — attitude in every line.

helpMemoryTips.title: 呢 keeps it warm
helpMemoryTips.text: The closing 我们还要再见面呢! carries a happy glow — 呢 softens a statement into shared excitement.

en_zh_b2_2_read_date.readingPassage:
小美的姐姐上个月认识了一个男孩子，两个人都喜欢爬山，很快就熟了。
第一次约会，男孩子七点就到了饭馆门口，站着等她。姐姐七点半才到，因为路上堵车堵得厉害。她远远地看见他手里拿着一束花，心里就不紧张了。
吃饭的时候，两个人聊得很开心。他不但会做菜，而且也喜欢看书。姐姐回家以后对小美说："只有跟他聊天的时候，我才觉得时间过得这么快。我们下星期还要再见面呢！"
en_zh_b2_2_read_date.readingPassageTranslation:
Last month Xiaomei's older sister met a boy; they both love hiking and quickly hit it off.
For the first date, the boy arrived at the restaurant at seven already and stood waiting. The sister didn't arrive until half past — the traffic jam was terrible. From a distance she saw the bouquet in his hand, and her nerves melted away.
Over dinner the two talked happily. He not only cooks, but loves books too. Back home, the sister told Xiaomei: "Only when I'm talking with him does time pass this fast. We're meeting again next week!"

readingQuestions.question: 男孩子几点到的？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What time did the boy arrive?

en_zh_b2_2_read_phones.title: Reading: 手机与生活
en_zh_b2_2_read_phones.helpMemoryIntro: Modern China through this module's grammar: 着-states everywhere, 一边…一边, 只有…才, and a 谁…谁 pattern worth stealing.

helpMemoryTips.title: 谁…谁… = whoever
helpMemoryTips.text: 谁先拿手机，谁就请客 — whoever grabs the phone first, THAT person treats. The question word doubles as "whoever" (Z28).

en_zh_b2_2_read_phones.readingPassage:
在中国，手机几乎就是生活本身。人们用手机买东西、点外卖、坐地铁、看病挂号。汤姆刚来的时候还带着钱包，现在他出门只带手机——钱包在家里放着，已经放了半年了。
手机让生活变得方便，可是也带来了新问题。在地铁里，几乎每个人都低着头看手机；朋友们坐在一起吃饭，也常常是一边吃着饭，一边看着手机。
小美说："我们只有把手机放下，才能真正地在一起。"所以他们约好：吃饭的时候，谁先拿手机，谁就请客。这个办法听起来简单，可是很有用——即使是最爱看手机的朋友，也坚持下来了。
en_zh_b2_2_read_phones.readingPassageTranslation:
In China, the phone practically IS daily life. People use it to shop, order food, ride the metro, register at the hospital. When Tom first arrived he still carried a wallet; now he leaves home with only his phone — the wallet has been sitting at home for half a year.
Phones make life convenient, but they bring new problems. On the metro, almost everyone rides with head bowed over a screen; friends sitting down to dinner often eat with one eye on their phones.
Xiaomei says: "Only by putting the phones down can we truly be together." So they made a deal: at dinner, whoever reaches for their phone first pays the bill. It sounds simple, but it works — even the most phone-addicted friend has stuck to it.

readingQuestions.question: 汤姆现在出门带什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Tom take when he goes out now?

readingQuestions.question: 朋友们约好了什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What deal did the friends make?

en_zh_b2_2_speak_flow.title: Speaking: connected speech at pace

subjects.english: Tā xiào zhe shuō: "Wǒmen zǒu ba!" — She said, smiling: "Let's go!"

en_zh_b2_2_speak_flow.helpMemoryIntro: Full sentences at natural speed: keep the particles light, the tones intact, and breathe at the commas.

helpMemoryTips.title: Light ≠ lost (Z6)
helpMemoryTips.text: 了, 着, 吧, 呢 go quiet and quick — but never vanish. Aim for "small but there": native rhythm keeps every syllable's slot.

en_zh_b2_2_speak_particles.title: Speaking: attitude particles 吧 / 呢 / 啊

subjects.english: Nǐ shì xuésheng ba? — You're a student, right?
Wǒ de yàoshi ne? — And where are my keys?
Zhè ge cài zhēn hǎochī a! — This dish is SO good!
Xiūxi yíxià ba. — Take a break, why don't you.

en_zh_b2_2_speak_particles.helpMemoryIntro: One syllable of attitude: 吧 suggests or guesses, 呢 muses "and…?", 啊 warms and exclaims. Say them lightly — they ride the sentence's tail.

helpMemoryTips.title: The tail carries the tone of voice
helpMemoryTips.text: 走吧 let's go (suggestion) · 你是学生吧? you're a student, right? (guess) · 我的书呢? and where's my book? · 真好啊! how nice! All neutral-toned, all attitude.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 又 looks back, 再 looks forward (Z27)
helpMemoryTips.text: 又迟到了 — late AGAIN (it happened). 再说一遍 — say it again (please, in the future). 再见 = see you again — future, hence 再.

en_zh_b2_2_zhe.helpMemoryIntro: Verb + 着 zhe freezes an action into a state: 门开着 the door stands open, 她穿着红衣服 she's wearing red. Also: V1着 V2 — doing B while A-ing.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ 着 = the pause button (Z16)
helpMemoryTips.text: 开 is opening; 开着 is standing open. 了 stamps the change, 着 holds the resulting state. 墙上挂着一张照片 — a photo hangs on the wall.

helpMemoryTips.title: V着 + V = while
helpMemoryTips.text: 她笑着说 she said, smiling; 我们坐着聊天 we sat chatting. The 着-verb paints the backdrop of the main verb.

en_zh_c1_1_attributives.helpMemoryIntro: Formal Chinese stacks whole layers before a noun: 一个对中国文化非常感兴趣的英国学生 — an English student deeply interested in Chinese culture. Build them layer by layer.

helpMemoryTips.title: Order inside the stack (Z19)

en_zh_c1_1_chengyu.helpMemoryIntro: 成语 are four-character set phrases — compressed stories that educated Chinese sprinkles everywhere. Start with six you can actually use.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Unpack the four characters (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 入乡随俗 enter-village-follow-customs = when in Rome. 半途而废 half-road-then-quit = give up halfway. Decode character by character and the phrase sticks.

helpMemoryTips.title: Placement matters
helpMemoryTips.text: Most 成语 slot in as predicates or adverbs: 他做事总是马马虎虎 (careless). Don't force them where a plain word belongs — sprinkled, not shoveled.

en_zh_c1_1_jiran.helpMemoryIntro: Reasoning tools: 既然…就 (since it's the case…), 否则 (otherwise), and the soft conditional tail …的话.

helpMemoryTips.title: 既然 ≠ 因为 (Z25)
helpMemoryTips.text: 因为 gives a cause; 既然 leans on a fact both sides already accept: 既然你来了，就坐下吧 — since you're here anyway. It still wants its 就/也.

en_zh_c1_1_listen_environment.title: Listening: 访谈 — 环境
en_zh_c1_1_listen_environment.helpMemoryIntro: An interview in educated, natural register — 越…越, 造成, 既然, and the rhetoric of advice.

helpMemoryTips.title: 从小事做起
helpMemoryTips.text: "Start from the small things" — 从 X 做起 is a set frame for advice; you'll meet it in every Chinese speech about change.

en_zh_c1_1_listen_environment.readingPassage:
记者："李老师，您做环保工作二十年了。在您看来，最大的变化是什么？"
李老师："最大的变化是人们的态度。二十年前，很多人觉得环保跟自己没关系。现在，垃圾分类、少用塑料袋，已经成了很多家庭的习惯。"
记者："那么，最让您担心的问题是什么？"
李老师："是速度。经济发展得越快，对环境的压力就越大。如果我们只顾眼前的利益，就会给下一代造成无法挽回的损失。"
记者："对于普通人，您有什么建议？"
李老师："从小事做起。既然改变世界很难，那就先改变自己的生活方式。"
en_zh_c1_1_listen_environment.readingPassageTranslation:
Reporter: "Teacher Li, you've worked in environmental protection for twenty years. In your view, what's the biggest change?"
Li: "The biggest change is people's attitude. Twenty years ago, many felt the environment had nothing to do with them. Now sorting waste and cutting plastic bags are habits in many households."
Reporter: "And what worries you most?"
Li: "Speed. The faster the economy grows, the greater the pressure on the environment. If we only mind immediate gains, we'll cause the next generation irreversible losses."
Reporter: "Any advice for ordinary people?"
Li: "Start small. Since changing the world is hard, first change your own way of living."

readingQuestions.question: 李老师觉得最大的变化是什么？
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What does Li see as the biggest change?

en_zh_c1_1_listen_lecture.title: Listening: 讲座 — 城市化
en_zh_c1_1_listen_lecture.helpMemoryIntro: A university-style lecture: the formal register in action — 使, 由于, 对于, 关于, 令人, 既…也.

helpMemoryTips.title: 既…也 = both…and (formal)
helpMemoryTips.text: 既带来了机会，也带来了挑战 — the written cousin of 又…又, joining two verb phrases in balanced style (Z30).

en_zh_c1_1_listen_lecture.readingPassage:
各位同学，下午好。今天我们谈谈城市化。
过去四十年，中国经历了世界上规模最大的城市化：几亿人从农村搬进了城市。城市化使经济快速发展，也使几亿人的生活水平得到了很大的提高。
但是，对于城市化，我们不能只看到好的一面。由于人口增长太快，一些大城市出现了交通拥堵、住房紧张等问题。另外，很多年轻人进城工作，农村只留下了老人和孩子，这也是一个令人担心的社会问题。
总的来说，城市化既带来了机会，也带来了挑战。关于怎么解决这些问题，我们下节课继续讨论。
en_zh_c1_1_listen_lecture.readingPassageTranslation:
Good afternoon, everyone. Today let's talk about urbanization.
Over the past forty years, China has gone through the largest urbanization in the world: hundreds of millions of people moved from the countryside into cities. Urbanization made the economy grow fast and greatly raised the living standards of hundreds of millions.
But we can't see only the good side. Because the population grew too fast, some big cities developed problems like traffic congestion and housing shortages. Also, with young people leaving for city jobs, only the old and the young remain in the villages — a worrying social problem.
All in all, urbanization brings both opportunities and challenges. As for how to solve these problems — we'll continue next class.

options: 世界上规模最大的城市化
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What has China gone through in the past forty years?

en_zh_c1_1_prepositions.helpMemoryIntro: The formal coverb set: 对/对于 toward (attitude), 关于 about (topic), 由于 owing to (cause). They frame the sentence before its verb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Aim, topic, cause (Z29)
helpMemoryTips.text: 对(于) aims an attitude at something; 关于 labels the topic (often fronted or in titles); 由于 gives the formal cause — and pairs happily with 因此.

en_zh_c1_1_read_essay.title: Reading: 一篇议论文
en_zh_c1_1_read_essay.helpMemoryIntro: A model argumentative essay: thesis, two supports, a concession, a turn — with 成语, 由于, 往往 and 反而 doing the heavy lifting.

helpMemoryTips.title: 欲速则不达
helpMemoryTips.text: "Desire speed, and you won't arrive" — a classical 成语 quoted mid-essay, exactly how educated prose deploys them (Z30).

en_zh_c1_1_read_essay.readingPassage:
在这个一切都追求"快"的时代，"慢"几乎成了一个贬义词。吃饭要快，走路要快，连休息都要"高效率"。然而，快真的总是好的吗？
首先，快容易使人马马虎虎。为了赶时间，我们常常把工作做得又快又糟，最后不得不花更多的时间去改正错误——欲速则不达，古人早就明白这个道理。
其次，快使我们失去了很多东西。由于急着赶路，我们看不见路边的风景；由于急着回消息，我们听不完朋友的一句话。生活的意义，往往就藏在这些被我们跳过的细节里。
当然，慢不等于懒。该快的时候快，该慢的时候慢，这才是真正的生活智慧。在人人都跑的时代，敢于慢下来，反而需要更大的勇气。
en_zh_c1_1_read_essay.readingPassageTranslation:
In an era that chases "fast" in everything, "slow" has almost become a dirty word. Eat fast, walk fast — even rest must be "efficient". But is fast really always good?
First, speed breeds carelessness. Racing the clock, we do our work fast and badly, then spend more time fixing the mistakes — "haste brings no arrival," as the ancients already knew.
Second, speed costs us things. Rushing down the road, we miss the scenery beside it; rushing to answer messages, we don't hear a friend finish a sentence. Life's meaning often hides in exactly the details we skip.
Of course, slow is not lazy. Fast when it should be fast, slow when it should be slow — that is real wisdom about living. In an age when everyone runs, daring to slow down takes the greater courage.

en_zh_c1_1_read_tech.title: Reading: 科技与生活
en_zh_c1_1_read_tech.helpMemoryIntro: An HSK-5-style essay: balanced argument, formal frames (使, 对于, 由于, 关于, 则, 反而), and a quotable conclusion.

helpMemoryTips.title: 反而 = contrary to expectation
helpMemoryTips.text: 老人…反而被挡在门外 — instead (of being helped), they're shut out. 反而 flags an outcome that flips what the setup promised.

en_zh_c1_1_read_tech.readingPassage:
过去十年，科技使我们的生活发生了巨大的变化。移动支付让钱包成为历史；网上购物使人们足不出户就能买到世界各地的商品；人工智能则开始进入医院、学校和家庭。
对于这些变化，人们的态度并不相同。支持者认为，科技提高了效率，使更多人享受到了方便的服务。由于看病可以网上挂号，农村的病人再也不用半夜排队了。
但也有人担心：老人学不会用智能手机，反而被新技术挡在了门外；年轻人越来越依赖手机，面对面的交流却越来越少。
关于科技，也许最重要的问题不是"它能做什么"，而是"我们想让它为我们做什么"。技术本身没有好坏，使用它的方式才决定它的价值。
en_zh_c1_1_read_tech.readingPassageTranslation:
Over the past decade, technology has transformed our lives. Mobile payment made wallets history; online shopping lets people buy goods from all over the world without leaving home; and artificial intelligence is entering hospitals, schools and homes.
Attitudes toward these changes differ. Supporters argue technology raises efficiency and brings convenient services to more people. Since hospital registration works online now, rural patients no longer queue at midnight.
But others worry: elderly people who can't master smartphones end up shut out by the new technology, and the young grow ever more dependent on their phones while face-to-face conversation shrinks.
Perhaps the most important question about technology is not "what can it do" but "what do we want it to do for us". Technology itself is neither good nor bad — how we use it decides its value.

readingQuestions.questionTranslation: What did mobile payment make history?

readingQuestions.question: 有人担心谁被新技术挡在门外？

readingQuestions.question: 文章认为，什么决定技术的价值？

en_zh_c1_1_shi_ling.helpMemoryIntro: Three ways to make something happen to someone: colloquial 让, formal 使, and 令 for triggered emotions (令人吃惊 — astonishing).

helpMemoryTips.title: Register picks the causative

en_zh_c1_1_speak_formal.title: Speaking: formal register delivery

subjects.display: 各位老师，各位同学，大家好。
subjects.english: Gèwèi lǎoshī, gèwèi tóngxué, dàjiā hǎo. — Teachers, fellow students: hello.

subjects.display: 今天我想谈谈科技对生活的影响。
subjects.english: Jīntiān wǒ xiǎng tán tán kējì duì shēnghuó de yǐngxiǎng. — Today I'd like to discuss technology's influence on life.

subjects.display: 由于时间有限，我只说三点。
subjects.english: Yóuyú shíjiān yǒuxiàn, wǒ zhǐ shuō sān diǎn. — As time is limited, I'll make three points.

subjects.display: 这个问题的重要性不言而喻。
subjects.english: Zhè ge wèntí de zhòngyàoxìng bùyán'éryù. — The importance of this issue goes without saying.
Xièxie dàjiā de qīngtīng. — Thank you all for listening.

en_zh_c1_1_speak_formal.helpMemoryIntro: Formal Mandarin is slower, evenly paced, fully toned — no swallowed syllables. Deliver these like a presenter.

helpMemoryTips.title: Formal = full syllables (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: Casual speech reduces; formal speech pronounces. Every 的, 了, 性 gets its full beat. Slow is not unnatural here — it's the register.

en_zh_c1_1_speak_opinion.title: Speaking: presenting an opinion

subjects.display: 在我看来，这个问题并不简单。
subjects.english: Zài wǒ kàn lái, zhè ge wèntí bìng bù jiǎndān. — In my view, this problem is by no means simple.

subjects.display: 首先，我们应该听听不同的意见。
subjects.english: Shǒuxiān, wǒmen yīnggāi tīng tīng bùtóng de yìjiàn. — First, we should hear different opinions.
Lìngwài, zhè yě shì yí ge jīhuì. — Besides, this is also an opportunity.

subjects.display: 当然，每个人的情况不一样。
subjects.english: Dāngrán, měi ge rén de qíngkuàng bù yíyàng. — Of course, everyone's situation differs.

subjects.display: 总的来说，我同意这个看法。
subjects.english: Zǒng de lái shuō, wǒ tóngyì zhè ge kànfǎ. — All in all, I agree with this view.

en_zh_c1_1_speak_opinion.helpMemoryIntro: The skeleton of a spoken argument: state, support, concede, conclude — in connected, natural Mandarin.

helpMemoryTips.title: Signpost, then speak
helpMemoryTips.text: 在我看来 / 首先 / 另外 / 总的来说 — plant a signpost at each turn. Chinese listeners navigate arguments by these markers (Z30).

en_zh_c1_1_synonyms_1.helpMemoryIntro: HSK 5 lives on pairs that translate identically but behave differently: one takes an object, the other splits; one is an adjective too, the other only an adverb.

helpMemoryTips.title: Test the grammar, not the gloss
helpMemoryTips.text: 帮助 + person (帮助我); 帮忙 splits and takes none (帮我一个忙). 突然 can be an adjective (很突然); 忽然 only ever an adverb. The dictionary meaning is the same — the syntax isn't.

helpMemoryTips.title: More pairs on this shelf
helpMemoryTips.text: 常常 (often, habits) vs 往往 (tends to, patterns + conditions); 一定 (must/surely) vs 肯定 (certainly, can be a verb: 我肯定…).

en_zh_c1_1_word_building.helpMemoryIntro: Three suffixes unlock hundreds of abstract words: 化 -ization (现代化), 性 -ness/-ity (重要性), 主义 -ism (乐观主义).

helpMemoryTips.title: Abstract building blocks (Z7)
helpMemoryTips.text: 全球 globe + 化 = globalization; 可能 possible + 性 = possibility; 现实 reality + 主义 = realism. Spot the suffix, decode the stem — free vocabulary at C1 scale.

en_zh_c1_2_bigtext_formal.title: Big text: a report in 书面语
en_zh_c1_2_bigtext_formal.helpMemoryIntro: A campus report with its register words removed. For each gap, pick the form that keeps the whole text in 书面语 — the casual twin is always lurking among the options.

helpMemoryTips.title: Register is a system (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: One 可是 in a report of 然而s breaks the suit. Choose by register first, grammar second — every option is grammatical, only one is dressed right.

en_zh_c1_2_bigtext_formal.readingTitle: 关于图书馆使用情况的报告
en_zh_c1_2_bigtext_formal.readingPassage:
关于图书馆使用情况的报告

本学期，图书馆的使用情况有了明显改善。与去年相比，每日到馆人数增长了三分之一。其中，周末的阅览室最受学生欢迎，常常座无虚席。
调查显示，大部分学生对新的开放时间表示满意，然而，也有部分同学建议，考试期间应将开放时间延长至晚上十一点。此外，自习区的座位仍然不足，高峰时段约有五分之一的学生找不到座位。
因此，我们建议：第一，增设两百个自习座位；第二，考试期间延长开放时间；第三，所有新措施均于下月起实行。
en_zh_c1_2_bigtext_formal.readingPassageTranslation:
Report on library usage

This semester, library usage has clearly improved. Compared with last year, daily visits grew by one third. The weekend reading rooms are the most popular with students — often not an empty seat.
Surveys show most students are satisfied with the new opening hours; however, some suggest extending opening to 11 p.m. during exams. Furthermore, study-area seats remain insufficient: at peak times about one fifth of students cannot find a seat.
We therefore recommend: first, adding 200 study seats; second, longer hours during exams; third, all new measures to take effect from next month.

en_zh_c1_2_dict_formal.helpMemoryIntro: Formal sentences at broadcast pace. The written function words (将, 于, 均, 由) are short — but your IME knows them if you type the whole phrase.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ jiāng/jiàng, yú/yǔ

en_zh_c1_2_discourse.helpMemoryIntro: The written connective set: 然而 however, 因此 therefore, 此外 furthermore, 总之 in short — the skeleton of every essay and report.

helpMemoryTips.title: Match register across the sentence (Z25/Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 然而 belongs with 将/由/之; 可是 belongs with 把/在/的. Mixing (然而…啦!) jars like "however… gonna". Pick a register, keep it.

en_zh_c1_2_formal_passive.helpMemoryIntro: Written Chinese has a passive palette: neutral 由 (handled by), receptive 受 (受到欢迎 well received), adverse 遭 (遭到破坏 suffered damage).

helpMemoryTips.title: Pick by flavour (Z23/Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 由 assigns responsibility, no drama: 会议由王教授主持. 受(到) receives, neutral-to-good: 受到好评. 遭(到) suffers, always bad: 遭到拒绝. 被 stays the everyday generalist.

en_zh_c1_2_jiang_yu.helpMemoryIntro: News and reports swap everyday words for classical ones: 将 replaces 把 (and marks futures), 于 replaces 在 for time and place.

helpMemoryTips.title: Two 将s, one 于 (Z30)
helpMemoryTips.text: 将 №1 = written 把: 请将手机关闭. 将 №2 = will: 会议将于九点举行. 于 = at/in/on after the verb or before the time: 生于1990年, 将于明日开幕.

helpMemoryTips.title: ⚠️ Don't speak the written words
helpMemoryTips.text: 将/于/之 in casual conversation sounds like reading a news bulletin at dinner. Register runs both ways — these are for writing and formal speech only.

en_zh_c1_2_listen_business.title: Listening: 商务会谈
en_zh_c1_2_listen_business.helpMemoryIntro: Polite business Mandarin: 贵公司, 百忙之中, hedged objections with 恐怕, and a 由-passive in action.

helpMemoryTips.title: 贵 = your (honorable)
helpMemoryTips.text: 贵公司 your (esteemed) company, 贵姓? your honorable surname? — the politeness prefix that makes business Chinese purr.

en_zh_c1_2_listen_business.readingPassage:
"李总，欢迎欢迎！感谢您百忙之中抽时间与我们见面。"
"张经理客气了。贵公司的方案我们已经仔细研究过了。"
"您觉得怎么样？"
"总的来说，方案十分专业。不过，恐怕有两点需要再商量：第一，交货时间太紧，我们希望能延长两周；第二，关于售后服务的条款，写得不够具体。"
"您提的这两点都很有道理。这样吧，交货时间我们可以调整，售后条款今天下午就由法务部重新起草，明天发给贵公司。"
"好，那就这么定了。合作愉快！"
"合作愉快！"
en_zh_c1_2_listen_business.readingPassageTranslation:
"Director Li, welcome! Thank you for making time to meet us out of your busy schedule."
"You're too kind, Manager Zhang. We have studied your company's proposal carefully."
"What do you think?"
"Overall, it's very professional. But I'm afraid two points need more discussion: first, the delivery schedule is too tight — we'd like two more weeks; second, the after-sales clauses aren't specific enough."
"Both points are fair. How about this: we can adjust the delivery time, and our legal department will redraft the after-sales clauses this afternoon and send them to you tomorrow."
"Good, it's settled then. To a happy cooperation!"
"To a happy cooperation!"

en_zh_c1_2_listen_news.title: Listening: 新闻播报
en_zh_c1_2_listen_news.helpMemoryIntro: Two broadcast news items — 将于, 由…组成, 均, 之美: the written register read aloud, exactly as Chinese TV does nightly.

helpMemoryTips.title: 均 = written 都
helpMemoryTips.text: 所有活动均免费 — all events are free. 均 is 都 in a suit; you'll hear it only in announcements and read it everywhere (Z30).

en_zh_c1_2_listen_news.readingPassage:
晚上好，欢迎收看晚间新闻。
第一条：本市地铁五号线将于下月正式开通。新线路全长四十二公里，由二十八个车站组成。专家认为，五号线的开通将大大缓解市中心的交通压力。
第二条：本周末，第十二届国际图书节将在市图书馆举行。届时，来自三十多个国家的作家将与读者见面。本届图书节的主题为"阅读之美"。组织者表示，所有活动均免费向公众开放，详情可在图书馆网站查询。

Good evening, and welcome to the evening news.
Item one: the city's Metro Line 5 will officially open next month. The new line runs 42 kilometres and consists of 28 stations. Experts believe its opening will greatly ease traffic pressure downtown.
Item two: this weekend, the 12th International Book Festival will be held at the city library. Writers from more than thirty countries will meet readers. This year's theme is "The Beauty of Reading". The organizers say all events are open to the public free of charge; details on the library's website.
