helpMemoryTips.title: 评论修辞（Z31）
helpMemoryTips.text: 对偶（best of times / worst of times）；比喻（leave a door open）；intrigue ≠ confusion 的辨析。

zh_en_c2_2_listen_critical.readingPassage: What makes a great opening line? Consider the famous first sentence: 'It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.' In just ten words, Dickens captures an entire age of contradiction. A great opening does not merely begin a story; it makes a promise to the reader. It says: trust me, this will be worth your time. Modern writers, under pressure to grab attention, sometimes forget that intrigue is not the same as confusion. The best openings are clear, yet they leave a door slightly open — a question we cannot help but want answered.
zh_en_c2_2_listen_critical.readingPassageTranslation: 什么造就了精彩的开篇句？想想那句著名的开头：「这是最好的时代，也是最坏的时代。」仅仅十个词，狄更斯就道尽了一个充满矛盾的时代。伟大的开篇不只是开始一个故事，它是对读者的一个承诺，它在说：相信我，这值得你花时间。现代作家在吸引眼球的压力下，有时忘了「引人入胜」不等于「令人困惑」。最好的开篇是清晰的，却留了一道微微敞开的门——一个我们忍不住想知道答案的问题。

zh_en_c2_2_listen_debate.readingPassage: Tonight's motion: 'This house believes that social media does more harm than good.' Speaking for the motion: 'We have created a world in which teenagers compare their real lives to the edited highlights of others, and then wonder why they feel inadequate. That is not connection; it is a slow poison.' And against: 'Every new technology has been feared. Social media has given a voice to the voiceless and toppled dictators. To blame the tool for how some use it is both lazy and dangerous.' A powerful exchange. Now, over to our audience.
zh_en_c2_2_listen_debate.readingPassageTranslation: 今晚的辩题：「本方认为社交媒体弊大于利。」正方发言：「我们造就了这样一个世界：青少年拿自己真实的生活去和别人经过修饰的高光片段比较，然后纳闷自己为何感到不如人。那不是连接，而是一种慢性毒药。」反方：「每一项新技术都曾被恐惧。社交媒体给了无声者以声音，也曾推翻独裁者。因为有些人的滥用就去责怪工具本身，既懒惰又危险。」精彩的交锋。现在，交给现场观众。

zh_en_c2_2_read_analysis.readingPassage: The numbers, at first glance, tell a reassuring story: unemployment is at a record low. Politicians have, predictably, rushed to take the credit. Look closer, however, and the picture grows murkier. Much of this 'employment' consists of insecure, part-time work, often paying less than a living wage. A person delivering parcels for twelve hours a day, with no sick pay and no guaranteed hours, counts in the statistics as 'employed' — and yet may be poorer than someone officially out of work a decade ago. Statistics, as ever, are not lies; but they are rarely the whole truth. The real question is not how many people are working, but whether that work allows them to live with dignity.
zh_en_c2_2_read_analysis.readingPassageTranslation: 乍看之下，数字讲述着一个令人安心的故事：失业率处于历史低位。不出所料，政客们争相邀功。然而，凑近一看，图景就变得模糊。许多所谓的「就业」是不稳定的兼职，报酬常常低于维生工资。一个每天送十二小时快递、没有病假、也没有保障工时的人，在统计里算作「就业」——却可能比十年前一个正式失业的人还要穷。数字，一如既往，并非谎言；但它们很少是全部真相。真正的问题不在于有多少人在工作，而在于那份工作能否让他们有尊严地生活。

helpMemoryTips.text: 'sell it by the weekend / by the hour'（对偶）；'screens murmur'（拟人）；含蓄有力的结语。

zh_en_c2_2_read_capstone.readingPassage: For most of human history, silence was free and abundant. Today, it has become a luxury. In our cities, the hum of traffic never truly stops; in our homes, screens murmur through the night. We have, without quite deciding to, engineered a world in which quiet is something we must actively seek out — and pay for. Wellness retreats sell it by the weekend; noise-cancelling headphones sell it by the hour. Yet the deeper cost may be one we have barely begun to measure. Studies increasingly suggest that constant noise raises stress, disturbs sleep, and erodes our very capacity to think. Perhaps the most radical act of the coming century will not be to speak louder, but to learn, once again, how to be still.
zh_en_c2_2_read_capstone.readingPassageTranslation: 在人类历史的大部分时间里，寂静是免费而充裕的。今天，它却成了一种奢侈。在城市里，车流的嗡鸣从未真正停止；在家中，屏幕彻夜低语。我们并未真正下过决心，却造出了这样一个世界：安静成了必须主动去寻找——而且要花钱买——的东西。养生营按周出售它，降噪耳机按小时出售它。然而更深的代价，也许是我们才刚刚开始衡量的。越来越多的研究表明，持续的噪音会增加压力、扰乱睡眠，并侵蚀我们思考的能力本身。也许，下一个世纪最激进的举动，不是把话说得更响，而是重新学会——如何安静下来。

readingQuestions.question: What does the writer suggest about noise?
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: 作者暗示噪音有什么影响？

readingQuestions.question: What is the writer's closing idea?
options: Learning to be still is radical
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: 作者结尾的观点是什么？

zh_en_c2_2_read_story.title: 阅读：Analysing a short story
zh_en_c2_2_read_story.helpMemoryIntro: 读一段关于短篇小说的文学分析。留意「留白」与含蓄的力量。

helpMemoryTips.title: 文学分析（Z31）
helpMemoryTips.text: 被动（nothing is explained, it has been said）；'white space' 的隐喻；含蓄胜过直白。

zh_en_c2_2_read_story.readingPassage: In Hemingway's famous six-word story — 'For sale: baby shoes, never worn' — nothing is explained, and yet everything is felt. The power lies entirely in what is left unsaid. We are not told who is selling the shoes, or why they were never worn; but the reader's imagination fills the silence with loss. This is the essence of great short fiction: it trusts the reader. Rather than describing grief, Hemingway hands us a single object and lets us feel its weight. The best stories, it has been said, are written as much in the white space between the words as in the words themselves.
zh_en_c2_2_read_story.readingPassageTranslation: 在海明威著名的六词小说——「出售：婴儿鞋，从未穿过」——中，什么都没有解释，却什么都感受到了。力量完全在于「没说出口」的部分。我们不知道是谁在卖这双鞋，也不知道它为何从未被穿过；但读者的想象把这段沉默填满了失去。这正是伟大短篇小说的精髓：它信任读者。海明威没有描写悲伤，而是递给我们一件小小的物品，让我们自己去感受它的重量。有人说，最好的故事，写在词与词之间的留白里，不亚于写在词句本身。

readingQuestions.question: What is special about the six-word story?
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: 这个六词故事特别在哪里？

readingQuestions.question: What does great short fiction do?
readingQuestions.questionTranslation: 伟大的短篇小说会做什么？

zh_en_c2_2_rhetoric.title: 修辞手法

subjects.display: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。
问题不是要不要，而是何时。
问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶）
这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。
轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵）
排比：政府民有、民治、民享。
低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气）
对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。
反问：我们还要再等多少年？
三段排比：更快、更高、更强。

sentences.sentence: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。 → I came, I saw, I ____.
sentences.english: 我来了，我看见了，我征服了。

sentences.sentence: 这可不是小事。 → This is ____ small matter.
问题不是要不要，而是何时。 → The question is not ____, but when.
sentences.english: 问题不是要不要，而是何时。
sentences.referenceExample: The question is not **whether**, but when.

sentences.sentence: 要么现在，要么永不。 → It is now or ____.
不自由，毋宁死。 → Give me liberty, or give me ____.
sentences.referenceExample: Give me liberty, or give me **death**.

sentences.sentence: 问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶） → Ask ____ you can do for your country.
sentences.english: 问问你能为国家做什么。（对偶）
sentences.referenceExample: Ask **what** you can do for your country.

sentences.sentence: 说来容易，做来难。 → Easier said than ____.
这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。 → This is not the end, nor even the beginning of the ____.
sentences.english: 这不是结束，甚至不是结束的开始。
sentences.referenceExample: This is not the end, nor even the beginning of the **end**.

sentences.sentence: 轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵） → It is a ____ on the expensive side.
sentences.english: 轻描淡写：这有点小贵。（其实很贵）
sentences.referenceExample: It is a **little** on the expensive side.

sentences.sentence: 我们越少谈论它越好。 → The less said about it, the ____.
sentences.referenceExample: The less said about it, the **better**.

sentences.sentence: 排比：政府民有、民治、民享。 → Government of the people, by the people, for the ____.
sentences.english: 排比：政府民有、民治、民享。
sentences.referenceExample: Government of the people, by the people, for the **people**.

sentences.sentence: 低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气） → He was ____ exactly pleased with the result.
sentences.english: 低调陈述：他对结果不太满意。（其实很生气）
sentences.referenceExample: He was **not** exactly pleased with the result.

sentences.sentence: 对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。 → We want bridges, not ____.
sentences.english: 对比：我们要的是桥梁，不是高墙。

sentences.sentence: 反问：我们还要再等多少年？ → How many more years must we ____?
sentences.english: 反问：我们还要再等多少年？
sentences.referenceExample: How many more years must we **wait**?

sentences.sentence: 三段排比：更快、更高、更强。 → Faster, higher, ____.
sentences.english: 三段排比：更快、更高、更强。

zh_en_c2_2_rhetoric.helpMemoryIntro: 排比、对偶、低调陈述等修辞让语言更有感染力。

helpMemoryTips.title: 修辞（Z31）
helpMemoryTips.text: 排比（I came, I saw, I conquered）、低调陈述（no small matter = 大事）、对比。

zh_en_c2_2_speak_capstone.title: 开口说：Capstone — 就复杂议题表达观点

subjects.display: On this issue, my position is clear.
subjects.english: 关于这个问题，我的立场很明确。

subjects.display: While there is merit on both sides ...
subjects.english: 虽然双方都有合理之处……

subjects.display: Ultimately, it comes down to what kind of society we want to be.
subjects.english: 归根结底，这关乎我们想成为怎样的社会。

zh_en_c2_2_speak_capstone.helpMemoryIntro: 毕业级口语：综合运用观点框架、让步、证据和有力的结语，完成一次完整的论述。

helpMemoryTips.title: 一次完整的论述（Z9）
helpMemoryTips.text: 立场 → 让步 → 证据 → 结论。用坚定而有分寸的语气收束——这是 C2 的标志。

zh_en_c2_2_speak_rebuttal.title: 开口说：即兴论辩与反驳

subjects.display: I take your point, but consider this ...
subjects.english: 我明白你的意思，但请考虑……
那正好证明了我的观点。

subjects.display: We must draw a distinction here ...
With respect, that simply doesn't hold up.

zh_en_c2_2_speak_rebuttal.helpMemoryIntro: 即兴反驳要礼貌而坚定，用连接语争取思考时间。听并跟读。

helpMemoryTips.title: 反驳的艺术（Z10）
helpMemoryTips.text: 先承认，再转折，最后立论：I take your point, but… On the contrary…。

zh_en_c2_2_speak_speech.title: 开口说：发表一场演讲

subjects.display: Friends, today we stand at a crossroads.
subjects.english: 各位，今天我们站在十字路口。

subjects.display: We cannot, and we will not, back down.
subjects.english: 我们不能，也绝不会退缩。

subjects.display: This is the duty of our generation.
subjects.english: 这是我们这一代的责任。

zh_en_c2_2_speak_speech.helpMemoryIntro: 用排比、停顿和坚定的语调打动听众。听并跟读。

helpMemoryTips.title: 演讲的力量（Z9）
helpMemoryTips.text: 排比、留白、直呼听众、有力的结语——让语言产生感染力。

zh_en_c2_2_speaking_close.title: 结业对话：精通
zh_en_c2_2_speaking_close.helpMemoryIntro: 整门课的最后一场对话。你构建的一切，在一次谈话里。复制、开口、带回你的最后一个分数。

helpMemoryTips.title: 最后的建议
helpMemoryTips.text: 不要展示语言，去使用它。当你不再想着精通时，精通才显形。

speaking.topic: The final conversation: a wide-ranging, natural discussion moving between registers — small talk, a debate, a story with irony, and a formal summing-up — as one continuous conversation. Show everything.
practisePoints: Register switching on demand, mid-conversation
Rhetorical structure in the summing-up
Idiom, understatement and precise modality
The near-native details: articles, third-person -s, final consonants
scoringCriteria: The conversation feels effortless, not performed
priorityErrors: the classic survivors: dropped articles and -s endings

zh_en_c2_2_speaking_mid.title: 对话：当编辑
zh_en_c2_2_speaking_mid.helpMemoryIntro: 中段检查点：这次你来当编辑，把臃肿的句子当场改好。复制、开口、把分数输回来。

helpMemoryTips.title: 先找动词
helpMemoryTips.text: 几乎每个臃肿的句子里都埋着一个被名词困住的动词。把它挖出来，句子自己就好了。

speaking.topic: You are the editor: I will say bloated, clumsy or ambiguous sentences and you re-say each one better — tighter, clearer, in the right register — explaining your choice in one line.
practisePoints: Rewriting wordy sentences concisely on the spot
Choosing register deliberately and saying why
Precision vocabulary over general words
scoringCriteria: No meaning lost in the compression

zh_en_c2_2_tone.title: 语气与分寸的掌控

sentences.sentence: 庄重宣布（讣告语气） → It is with deep regret that we ____ ...
sentences.referenceExample: It is with deep regret that we **announce** ...

sentences.sentence: 轻松打趣 → Well, that could have gone ____!
外交辞令 → We have agreed to ____.
含蓄批评 → The report leaves something to be ____.
sentences.referenceExample: The report leaves something to be **desired**.

sentences.sentence: 真诚感谢 → Words cannot ____ my gratitude.
婉转拒绝 → I am afraid we must respectfully ____.
sentences.referenceExample: I am afraid we must respectfully **decline**.

sentences.sentence: 得体祝贺 → Please accept my warmest ____.
深切慰问 → Our thoughts are ____ the family.
克制的乐观 → There are grounds for cautious ____.
轻松自嘲 → Clearly, modesty is not my strong ____!
sentences.referenceExample: Clearly, modesty is not my strong **suit**!

sentences.sentence: 郑重承诺 → You have my ____.
委婉提醒 → With all due ____, that may not be accurate.
sentences.referenceExample: With all due **respect**, that may not be accurate.

sentences.sentence: 低调的自信 → I have every ____ in our team.
sentences.referenceExample: I have every **confidence** in our team.

sentences.sentence: 得体的道歉 → I owe you an ____.
克制的批评 → The performance fell ____ of expectations.

zh_en_c2_2_tone.helpMemoryIntro: 讣告的庄重、打趣的轻松、外交的含蓄——高级表达在于分寸。

helpMemoryTips.title: 分寸（Z32）
helpMemoryTips.text: 不同场合选择恰当的语气：庄重、含蓄、真诚或调侃，都靠固定表达来实现。
